the next big thing in 2023 for developers

A próxima tendência no mundo de Devs na América Latina em 2023 é

the next big thing in 2023 for developers is to leverage artificial intelligence in their workflows. New code, refactoring code and automated tests will be all generated by AI and just reviewed by developers. We are moving to much higher level “languages” like low-code and no-code. This new developer can be 1000x more productive than existing ones.

A próxima tendência no mundo de Devs em 2023 para os desenvolvedores é alavancar a inteligência artificial em seus fluxos de trabalho. Novo código, refatoração e testes automatizados serão todos gerados pela IA e apenas revisados pelos desenvolvedores. Estamos mudando para “linguagens” de muito mais alto nível, como low-code e no-code. Esse novo desenvolvedor pode ser 1000 vezes mais produtivo do que os existentes.

# A Failed Talk

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/a-failed-talk
Tags: talks, react

#talk #failure #form #formik #react

A talk is a good way to explain some concept.

When doing a talk you need to know your audience, you can't target beginners and advanced users at once

A failed talk can happen for many reason

- wrong subject
- bad slides/content
- wrong audience targeting

Substack

There are no hard subjects to be cover in a presentation, there are only different ways of presenting them.

I did a “bad” talk at Rancho Dev when I’ve talked about Forms and Formik (slides and code here).

The problem of this talk was about my assumptions of the audience. I’m used to talking in places that most people know basic React concepts, but Rancho Dev conf was a more broad conferences with many different topics.

As I did not provide more context (a basic intro of React, react hooks and so on), it was hard to explain to them how to apply this concepts to solve the forms in React land. I always ask for feedback ( give me here) after my talk, and this one I received a really bad one saying that I thought the audience won’t grasp the concepts.

The truth was that I didn’t understand really well these concepts to explain like I’m 5.

How would be a better talk for that audience?

- More about the problem and motivation (how hard complex forms can be to get right)
- basic React intro concepts
- more concepts less code

## Link

[Community](./community) you need to give talk to create a community

[Share](./share)

# A mock GraphQL service

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/a-mock-graphql-service
Tags: graphql, opensource

#idea #opensource #graphql

The idea is a simple Koa server that receives the schema.graphql in a body

applies the mocks to it, and return a given query

app.use(getSchemaFromBody())

app.use(graphql())

here is the demo

- https://github.com/sibelius/graphql-mock

it takes a schema and a mock resolvers definitions, and generate a GraphQL operation result based on this

# Abstract Node

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/abstract-node
Tags: learning, thinking

You can model knowledge as a graph of nodes of concepts/ideas

When you abstract 2 or more ideas in a more general concept finding the edges among those nodes

This will make show up a new node with the concept that can represent both type of knowledge

# Asynchronous Mentorship

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/asynchronous-mentorship
Tags: advice, mentorship

Most mentees belive that they need sync mentorship to be able to explain their problems.
However, I've found that doing an async mentorship using text to provide better results.
Mentorship is a long term process, you can't "fix" or "improve" someone in a session, it takes time.

![image](/img/mentorship.png)

## Mentorship Cycle
The mentee will pass in the 3 steps of the mentorship cycle. The first one is to be in a given situation, or having some problem or doubt.
The mentor will analyse and provide some advice and ideas based on his/her experience, thus unblocking the mentee to do more work.
After that, the mentee needs to work, read and reflect on ideas and advice, that will make him/her progress in his/her goals.

## Rules
- be proactive and active in twitter and discord, to bring new situations and problems to the mentor
- ask a lot of questions to guide you to find the answer you are looking for
- read everything that was recommended, code everything that is needed, apply advices to test if they work for you

## Start here

Start answering all these [questions](./mentorship-questions)

---

# Atom

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/atom
Tags: thinking, learning

#atom #thoughts

We can use atom to describe something that is minimal and indivisible

We can have an atom of state like redux recoiljs

We can have an atom of thought as Roam and Zettelkästen uses

We can derive state using multiple atoms

We can compose thoughts ideas using many atoms

A [Mental Models](./mental-models) is an atom of thought, very well defined one.

We can have `atomic` [CSS](./css) , to compose our styles

Atoms are the building blocks ([The era of Content Builders](./the-era-of-content-builders) , [Where good ideas come from](./where-good-ideas-come-from)) of everything

In design you have colors, space, fonts are the basic atoms/blocks to mix and match content

An audience is a group of people that is listen to a talk, that will use a product.

In the same way a talk can fail when targeting a wrong audience ([A Failed Talk](./a-failed-talk) ).

A product/service will fail if it target the wrong audience.

An audience is the market of your Product Market Fit, without it you won't go further and won't succeed ([How to be Successful](./how-to-be-successful) )

Learning in public is good to build your audience

- https://www.swyx.io/writing/learn-in-public/

Your audience will learn with you

You need to give a lot of good stuff for free

# backend hiring questions

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/backend-hiring-questions
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## backend questions

"Good backend hiring question?"

- how to scale backend? horizontal scaling, vertical scaling, caching, event driven, async job processing, queues
- how to optimize database queries? use indexes, use the explain command, simplify queries, use materialized views, cache
- what is idempotent ? a request that can be called multiple times without changing the result, a good example is a payment, if the payment is made twice, the result is the same
- how to make a function, request idempotent ? use an idempotency key, use an unique database index
- how to make a system fault-tolerant? use retries using async job processing, handle error properly, use error code.
- what to do when a webhook that you are waiting for does not arrive? create a pooling fallback
- how to document backend archicture? use diagrams, state machine, sequence diagram
- when to use a state machine? when you have a complex flow, like a payment, a subscription, a user registration
- how to ensure the data system is consistent? create auditing tools to validate this, use state machines
- how to test backend ? prefer integration tests like test input and output of API, GraphQL, jobs, database state avoid mocking databases.
- how to implement event driven ? use a message broker like kafka, rabbitmq, sqs, sns, redis, bull
- how to decouple backend ? create packages/repository per domain instead of feature, avoid circular dependencies, use event-driven
- how to automate ci/cd? use github actions, gitlab ci, circle ci, jenkins, travis, docker, docker-compose, kubernetes
- why observability is important? to understand the system, to understand the user, to understand the business, to understand the performance
- how to implement observability ? apm, prometeus, sentry, grafana, tracing, metrics and logs
- how to deploy backend? pure ec2, vps, eks, k8s, aws, gcp, azure, heroku, netlify, vercel, digital ocean
- how to do data modelling ? prefer simpler models over complex models, fewer models and fields are better, prefer to avoid too many relationship and joins
- when to use docker and docker compose ? to automate deployment and simplify dx for development
- how to do database migrations? for sql you need structural and data migrations, for nosql you need to create a new collection and migrate the data
- when to use cache ? to cache expensive operations, to cache oauth token with expirations
- how to deal with eventual consistency? avoid read followed by write, read from primary, improve write and read concern
- how to deal with distributed systems? use idempotent, use retries, use async job processing, use queues, use event-driven, use state machines
- how to deal with external APIs? decouple the external API using port adapters, have a fallback for an API
- how to deal with concurrency to update a shared resource like a ledger balance? conditional put, locks, database transactions
- when to use REST API or GraphQL ? prefer GraphQL for internal products, and REST API for public APIs.
- how to deal with security? use oauth, use jwt, use https, use cors, use csrf, use rate limit, use waf, use security
- vercel vs serverless vs k8s vs ec2 ? vercel for MVP, ec2 for simple workflows, prefer k8s for complex workflows and to be able to move from cloud providers/on-premise/bare-metal, prefer serverless for event-driven workflows

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/being-wrong
Tags: thinking, learning

#wrong #fail

You can be wrong in many situations

Make sure to always revalidate your ideas on new information like Bayesian approach

I was wrong about `Flow` , `Typescript` proved themself my better in short and long term.

I was wrong about `Flow` because I didn't give a real change for `Typescript` before working on a pull request for `peril/danger`

What else am I missing?

# Big O

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/big-o
Tags: algorithms, performance

Big O is how we measure how fast an algorithm is, and how fast it grows as the input N grows

O(n) means the algorithm increases at the same rate as their input

o(log n) means it increases based on their log (usually the depth of the tree), used on tree algorithms to [Search](./search) data

To improve performance we always try to find better algorithm with better times over number of inputs

Sometimes the way to solve this is to reduce the `input`, it is to process less or "cache" some results.

Like bazel or dynamic programming does

# Bitcoin

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/bitcoin
Tags: crypto, economics

- https://blog.keys.casa/the-dos-and-donts-of-bitcoin-key-management/

- https://www.amazon.com.br/Bitcoin-Standard-Decentralized-Alternative-Central-ebook/dp/B07BPM3GZQ

Sound money

sound/hard money is money that it is a good store of value, it does not suffer with inflation, and it can't be easily made

proof of work is about creating a decentralised timestamp server, where you know the order of events

it is about time.

- https://21lessons.com/
- https://dergigi.com/2021/01/14/bitcoin-is-time/

---

A bitcoin transaction can be made of many inputs and many outputs

an input is a uxto (unspendable transactions)

so if you have 10btc and you wanna transfer 1btc to someone, you generate 2 outputs, as the other one will be your "pocket" change

block explorer is like the index for the blockchain

info about a transaction

info about a transaction block (a block contains many transactions)

a coinbase in the first transaction of a new block that represents the fee of the miner

proof of work is just finding the correct nonce that generate the 2 sha256 hash with many 0 at first.

bitcoin script let you program bitcoin

multisig like 2-3 let 2 of 3 diginal signatures spend the transactions

lighthing network make it possible many transactions of chain

send a transaction with some value to bitcoin (multi sig), like 1 btc

after the offchain transaction is settle up, you commit a new transaction with refund based on other transactions.

payment channel.

bitcoin is like gold

gold is not good to handle payments

new generation of crypto, ethereum, smart contract, dai, nano.

- https://thegraph.com/

[https://getblock.io/](https://getblock.io/)

# Black Swan

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/black-swan
Tags: risk, books

Black swan is an unexpected event that causes massive consequences.

One event that usually happens on the tail of the propability.

The last black swan as covid19.

Covid19 is a new virus that has a high rate of contagious.

The dead rate is not too high (7%), but it is a new virus it can collapsible the health virus increasing the dead rate.

It changed the way society works, right now we work from home.

We stopped physical store opening.

- https://www.amazon.com.br/Black-Swan-Improbable-Robustness-Fragility/dp/081297381X

# Blank Canvas

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/blank-canvas
Tags: writing, creativity

#design #writing #creativity

A blank canvas is starting to do something out of nothing

It is very hard to build something without nothing to start with

The idea of Zettelkasten is to fill this canvas with your preprocessed notes, so you can just reorganized them to write the final text.

You're gonna have all the sources, quotes and material to mix and match to write the final text

Don't start from a Blank Canvas

# Bleeding edge

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/bleeding-edge
Tags: career, learning

#bleeding edge

Bleeding edge is the state of art of something

It is the new technology

When you focus on bleeding edge (new), you have an advantage as everybody start in a clean slate.

You are not competing with Java developers with 10 or more years of experience

Everybody using React hooks has only a few months of experience, so you can compete fair with them

It also show the value of niche, as most people won't try new tools until they gain traction

It can have a great upside if you are right, but the downside is not big as you can transfer the learning concepts to other projects.

## Reference

- https://www.swyx.io/writing/specialize-in-the-new

# Books as answers

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/books-as-answers
Tags: books, learning, mentorship

#book #answer #mentorship

I believe we can learn a lot in books.

We can learn knowledge that author took some years to figure it out in a few hours or days.

It is like compressing your learning

When someone ask me a question I usually answer with a book to be read

# Build Less

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/build-less
Tags: ci, monorepo, devops

monorepo testing and build playground

- https://github.com/sibelius/monorepo-101

- https://github.com/entria/entria-deploy

Tooling around Git and compare\_url to decide what to build

It does not matter if you have the fastest algorithm if your N is too big.

Sometimes you need to reduce N to make sure you sure things does not grow with N.

As your project grows, your "N" will grow together.

Your dependencies sizes will grow

Your codebase will grow

Your tests will grow (if you care about long term)

Your build process will slow down as you are building more code.

Your type checking will get slower.

One way to solve this is to use a directly acyclic graph (DAG) to avoid testing, type checking, rebuilding what has not changed since last time.

In this article we won't use a DAG, we are going to use a much simpler strategy that can be modify to add a DAG to make it more robust.

The first thing that we want to do is to only run tests that are affected by the current files.

How do we know which files were changed?

We are going to use some `git` commands to make this possible.

**CircleCI concepts**

CircleCI is a continuous integration system that let you automate common software tasks, for instance: linting, tests, type checking, build, deploy.

A new pipeline is trigged when you do some work (push a new commit, for instance).

A pipeline can contains many workflows.

Each workflow have jobs that represents the cycle of your software process (for instance, install → test → deploy).

A job contains N steps of commands to perform something, like run lint, run tests.

Compare URL

CircleCI had a concept of CIRCLECI\_COMPARE\_URL before v2.1, that you can recreate in v2.1 using pipeline variables, like this:

environment:

CIRCLE\_COMPARE\_URL: &lt;&lt; pipeline.project.git\_url >>/compare/&lt;&lt; pipeline.git.base\_revision >>...&lt;&lt;pipeline.git.revision>>

Here is a few examples of COMPARE\_URL:
[https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/...a2e2709c4](https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/...a2e2709c4)

The url above says that this pipeline contains code from the base branch (master or main) to the [`a2e2709c4`](https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/...a2e2709c4) commit.

[https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/37ac69404a5b...69bc6e3fe337](https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/37ac69404a5b...69bc6e3fe337)

The above contains code from commit `37ac69404a5b` to `69bc6e3fe337`.

Test by yourself here [https://github.com/sibelius/monorepo-101/compare/master...8f8760](https://github.com/sibelius/monorepo-101/compare/master...8f8760)

**Problems with CIRLCLE\_COMPARE\_URL using pipeline variables**

The first problem we hit when using CIRCLE\_COMPARE\_URL using pipeline variables was that they are only bringing the range from the current commit to the last commit.

We would like to always test files related to the whole changes in the pull requests.

To fix this, we discard the "base revision" (the first commit in the compare url), and use the base branch instead.

this

[https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/37ac69404a5b...69bc6e3fe337](https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/37ac69404a5b...69bc6e3fe337)

turns into

[https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/master...69bc6e3fe337](https://github.com/owner/repo/compare/37ac69404a5b...69bc6e3fe337)

Before getting the files using git diff (spoiler), we need to checkout the latest master.

This is needed because CircleCI only do a shallow checkout to make it faster, you don't need all git history or branches in every pipeline.

```bash
if [[ $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD) != "master" ]]; then
  git branch -f master origin/master;
fi
```

**Testing only affected test files**

After all this setup we need to get a list of all affected files to make sure we are testing the right amount of tests.

FILES\_CHANGED=$(yarn --silent entria-deploy changes $\{CIRCLE\_COMPARE\_URL\} --baseRef $\{BASE\_REF\})

We are using entria-deploy cli to helps us get a list of all files that changed using compare url and a base ref/branch.

What we are really just doing is a git diff —name-only, like this

git diff [master...8f8760](https://github.com/sibelius/monorepo-101/compare/master...8f8760) —name-only

that return a list of all files that changes, like this:

packages/packageB/src/index.ts

After this, we are going to use jest —findRelatedTests to find which testfiles to test

TESTFILES=$(yarn --silent jest --findRelatedTests --listTests $FILES\_CHANGED)

The result is for this example is this:

`packages/packageB/src/__tests__/packageB.spec.ts`

Before testing these files we need to check if there is any testfile to test, this could happen if you are only modifying [README.md](http://readme.md) or other files

```bash
if [ ! -z "$TESTFILES" ];
  then
    JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT="./packages/cores/test-results/jest/results.xml" yarn jest --passWithNoTests --coverage --forceExit --ci --maxWorkers=7 $TESTFILES
fi
```

Splitting tests to make them blazing fast

We can use `circleci tests split` to split test files to run them in parallel

```bash
TESTFILES_SPLITTED=$(echo $TESTFILES | circleci tests split | xargs -n 1 echo)
```

**Build and Deploy only affected packages**

After bringing down the testing time in pull requests to a mean of 3x, can we only build and deploy affected packages? sure we can.

Our monorepo contains many GraphQL servers, and some REST (just one I swear), we also have many frontends and many apps (some white labels).

We used to build and deploy all of them to staging on master after every commit.

To solve this, we used the CIRCLE\_COMPARE\_URL (that provides the right range in master), to check if we changed any file that would affected the package to be deployed.

```bash
SHOULD_BUILD=$(yarn --silent entria-deploy hasChanged $CIRCLE_COMPARE_URL packages/shared packages/api
echo $SHOULD_BUILD
if [ "$SHOULD_BUILD" == false ]; then
    circleci-agent step halt
fi
```

entria-deploy hasChanged is just

```bash
git diff master...8f8760 --name-only packages/shared packages/api
```

circleci-agent step halt

make the job stop, so we have one of this before each step of build/deploy to make sure we are not building and deploying something that haven't changed.

you also want to use less parallel testing if you need to test much less tests

5000 → 6 dockers

# Buying Time

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/buying-time
Tags: time

When I come back to São Paulo to make my internship at PontoTel Startup.

I could live in my parents house at Guarulhs for "free"

It would only take me 2 hours to go to work and 2 hours to go back home.

I would lose 4 hours per day commuting, 20 hours per week and 80 hours per month. That's 960 hours per year.

I knew that my time was my precious resource, so I decided to buy it.

If you do basic math, I work 8 hours per day, 5 days per week, 4 weeks per month, that's 160 hours per month.
I was earning R$1500.00, so my hour was R$9.35. I was losing 80 hours * R$9.35 = R$748 per month.

I found a room to rent in São Paulo for R$400.00 and used these extra 4 hours to study and work a lot. 

All these 4 hours paid off a lot. I was able to work more, study more and learn more.
I was also going to happy hours and networking events, which helped me to meet a lot of people.
Additionally, I was able to create a tech community and find my co-founder for my own Startup.

# certificates are worth

## certificates are worth

"Are there specific certifications or courses you would recommend to complement hands-on learning and personal projects?"

I prefer to learn from primary sources, and they are most books over courses on youtube, udemy.

Textbooks are great to learn from primary source.

You can learn from a variaty of sources like text, audio, video, books, courses, certificates.

You should focus more on learning and knowledge.

Prefer active learning methods where you need to do exercises, build something to validate that you are really learning.

The real value of the "certificate" is the knowledge that it will give you.

You only learn when doing, so do not focus a lot on getting the certificate badge.

# college or school of life

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/college-or-school-of-life
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## college or school of life

Do a College in these situations:

You don't have the discipline to learn by yourself
You are not used to self-taught
You are not getting a job
You and/or your family have enough money to sustain you for 4/5 years without earning a lot
Prefer to do Public College in Brazil like USP, Unicamp, they are the best.
You want to validate if you want to work in business or in research
You want to work in FAANG, Big Tech, or move abroad where they value and require a degree.
To get networking and friends and college experience.
This network can help you go higher in your carrer later on.

Do not do College in these situations, or for these reasons:

You just want a degree, the diploma.
You need money right it way
You are a self-taught
You already got a job as a developer

Prefer a technical course or a bootcamp if you wanna go to market fast.

Everything that you can learn on College you can learn outside college.
Go check the syllabus of the course and read the textbooks. Do the exercises to really learn

---

# common challenges for developers in the beginning

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/common-challenges-for-developers-in-the-beginning
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## common challenges for developers in the beginning

"What are the most common challenges faced by developers early in their career and how can I prepare myself to face them?"

One common challenge is to decide what kind of developer you want to be: backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, devops, other.

My advice is to be more generalist at the beginning of your carrer, test everything until you decide what you like more to do.

Another challenge is to be able to learn a lot of new things that come up every day.

My advice for this is to focus more on concepts over implementations. Concepts are much more stable than implementation.
HTML, CSS and JavaScript is much more stable than React.

Learn to be invariant to implementations: learn React, Angular, Vue, and make it easy to learn a new framework as they show up.
Learn databases, and be able to learn a new database faster.

Always focus on how can you learn a new thing faster.

Another challenge for juniors is to proof they are worth to hire.

My advice is to do everything in public. Write articles, Open source your code. Deploy to production.
You need proof of work. Get all public code challenges of companies that you want to work.
Study the companies and how that you can solve their problems.

You can also work for free to get experience

You need experience.
Use freelances or any work that show up to get experience

Contribute to open source to get experience

You need to master your tech tack, your IDE, terminal, automated testes, how to develop software properly with feature flags.

## References

<Embed url='https://twitter.com/sseraphini/status/1760262122129207442' />

# common mistakes of developers

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/common-mistakes-of-developers
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## common mistakes of developers

"What are common mistakes new developers make and how can I try to avoid them?"

Not focusing on programming fundamentals

Not doing a lot of logic exercises, LeetCode

Not learning algorithms and data structuring

Not learning programming paradigm - Object Oriented, Functional, Logic

Not learnig more than one programming language

Not learning more than one database

Not using and learning to use terminal

Not learn how to optimize their workflow, IDE

Not coding against automated tests

Not doing code review of everybody in their team

Not leading a project/product

Not leading a team

Only coding

Not writing RFC and POC before coding

Not writing articles

Not using Learning in Public

Not learn how to make module code and decoupled code

Not knowing system design, distributed system, and how to scale software

Not instrumenting coding

Not to be effective while debugging

Not thinking in code as input, transformations and output.

Not focusing on networking

Not focusing on community

Not focusing on social skills

Being bad at communication and argumentation.

Not making public talks.

Only doing what they already know. In fact, you should avoid doing everything that you already know how to do

Not getting more responsability

# Concepts over Implementation

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/concepts-over-implementation
Tags: concepts, implementation

## Prefer Concepts over Implementation

- babel -> compilers
- webpack -> bundlers
- javascript -> programming logic
- sql -> databases
- redis -> cache
- serverless, k8s, aws -> containers, linux, vm, DNS, IP
- express -> HTTP/TCP/UDP
- react -> html, css, js

# Constraint are good

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/constraint-are-good
Tags: architecture, design

Most people think about constraint in a bad way

I think constraint is good for many reasons

Constraints gives you a limited set of options to perform or use.

GraphQL is better than REST because it has more constraints, you can't do everything you want in GraphQL.

You can't ask any data, and you can't return any data. You need to think first in the structure of the data that you want to expose to end users.

Declarative provides a limit set of operations that you can perform.

When you move to imperative you can do anything, but I argue that you should avoid this to reduce complexity.

K8s declarative yaml are better than CDK before you can't do everything you want in your infra.

So it is easier to maintain in the long run.

Avoid trying to fix all edge cases in the low level building blocks.

Constraints limits complexity as you need to work with a limited set of options.

Constraints limit the number of [Abstractions](./abstractions) that you can use.

[Design System](./design-system) are constraints for your product UI, it does not let you do everything, as you want to keep consistency

Constraints are about consistency.

Habits are constraints to your daily life to make your more productive

Constraints are about less choices

Letting tools make decisions for you ([Defer Understand](./defer-understand) )

- https://www.jackfranklin.co.uk/blog/letting-tools-make-choices/

Building Block gives you a limited set of basic blocks to work on, if you need something that is not available in any block you have 2 options:

1. create a new block increasing complexity
2. try to rethink your current needs

# Core API

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/core-api
Tags: opensource, architecture

Building Block

Core API of any package should be very tiny

A tiny API is easier to reason about it

A tiny API is easier to maintain

A tiny API is easier to learn

Add extensions points to your API to make it extensions and cover all user needs

a tiny API is easier to make new releases

a tiny API needs less tests

What should be the core API of react-native-camera?

take a picture

render picture preview

record a video

What about filters in the photo? another package

What about MLKit like face-detection and text detection? 2 new packages

# Creation Process

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/creation-process
Tags: creativity, writing

Any creation process is easier if you not start from a "blank canvas"

When doing Writing it is better to start from writing pieces instead of pulling ideas out of your mind.

If you try to start writing directly from your mind, you need first to transform your mind ideas into text, and them combine them. Mind has a process as the ideas are not so structure, and also subjectivy

When starting coding, it is easier to start off from piece of code or boilerplate. It is easier to combine existing code with code that you're gonna build on the fly. Another benefit of using existing code, it the code worked before it has more changes to keep working now.

When doing design start with some basic elements, or existing design.

Modify to your requirements. It is much easier to combine pre-existent UI elements instead of drawing everything using a pencil.

What about creating a new music? or a remix? isn't it to start with some sounds and compose them?

What about video? you can have some set of images to compose in the video, some set of predefined animations, some set of short videos.

start from building blocks - [Where good ideas come from](./where-good-ideas-come-from)

# CSS

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/css
Tags: css, frontend, design

#css #style

Avoid having too much CSS/styles in the product code

Your [Design System](./design-system) should use functional css to make it possible to extend it

Your design system should have constraints to avoid bad design

The design system should be able to change theme colors, as customers usually customize the product to their brand and workflow

functional css is a much better abstraction then other css approaches

css in js is better because of colocation

styled-components is a component + style

address the naming problem

convention naming

naming pattern

styled-system and tailwind follow naming convention to build functional css and compose styling.

saas, css modules, less, BEM does not address this problems

The product code should just be the use of building blocks from the design system

There is no shortcut for CSS, CSS has a lot of details, you need to keep adding keys and learn how they interact with each other

The build blocks for layout are flexbox and css grid, you should learn both.

Learn CSS

Flexbox and CSS grid can solve most of the layout problems

- https://flexboxfroggy.com/
- https://cssgridgarden.com/

Prebuilt blocks

- https://github.com/mertJF/tailblocks

## References

# Culture

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/culture
Tags: culture, book

Culture is what people do when you are not looking

The culture is build based on what you do, not what you say.

A good culture is build on principles, not rules.

Rules are too strict, principles help people to make the right decisions.

# Deep Dive

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/deep-dive
Tags: learning

You can only deep dive if you know how to swim

You can learn advanced stuff if you haven’t mastered the basics

[Defer Understand](./defer-understand)

If you try to deep dive before learning to swimming you drown and feel bad about the learning experience.

When you are at the edge: [Bleeding edge](./bleeding-edge)

You need to deep dive as there is not much in the surface.

You need both holistic and deep dive details views of the problems to provide the best solutions to them.

A holistic only will miss important details that you can only see when you zoom in

If you only focus on small details you will be stuck in a local solution

---

# Defer Understand

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/defer-understand
Tags: learning

Defer is when you let something to do in the future

When learning something you don’t need to understand everything related to it

You can defer some parts to the future

When learning React, focus on React using create-react-app, an opinionated tool, first.

Defer Babel, webpack.

- https://www.jackfranklin.co.uk/blog/letting-tools-make-choices/

It does not mean that you don’t need to learn these stuff. It means you can go back to them when you get used to that you are learning.

Understanding is overrated, I don’t understand every single detail, I prefer to learn high level concepts first and then deep dive when needed

A good [Zine](./zine) for this is this one

---

# Derivative

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/derivative
Tags: thinking, math

If you studied calculus you know the concept of a derivative of a function.

I'm not a mathematician, my simple definition is that derivate of a function is the rate of change of a given point.

If you take the second derivate equal zero you can find the minimum and/or maximum of a function.

This is useful in machine learning where you want to optimize your loss function.

Gradient descent algorithm is basically calculate the gradient, derivates of all dimensions of your function, and move a bit in that direction that will let you find the zero of the function being optimized.

---

One thing that I like to do is to apply concepts of one area into another.

We can use derivative term as second order effects of a given fact.

What is the derivative of covid19?

Derivative in this phrase is all about what these changes will affect the world in the long run.

Let's derive some hypothesis:

Covid19 changed our society in many ways.

It changed how we worked, most of the companies moved to remote work to avoid contamination.

Some companies decided to be remote work only. Some companies decided to be remote forever.

What will happen in the long run? remote work will be more common, or we are going back to the office?

It affected a lot small business that only had a physical location to sell their goods. Some of them broke, some of them moved to sell their good using e-commerce with delivery for short location and shipping for big ones. Will all stores have a digital experience even when everything is back to "normal"?

it changed how students have to learn. As most schools moved to an online experience, most people feel that the "watching" is not enough to learn and master the subject, they were watching before inside a classroom.

# Design System

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/design-system
Tags: design, frontend

Design system contain the building blocks of UI elements/atoms to build your product UI

It should allow extensions using functional [CSS](./css)

Design system should define list of fonts

Design system should define list of possible spacing (so everything is spaced with the same style)

Design system is about constraint, you limit what you can do to avoid creating weird UI, and keep consistency

# Dichotomy

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/dichotomy
Tags: thinking, programming

Dichotomy is to divide the whole in 2 parts

We have many dichotomies in life and in code

server/client → we want to do some work on the server and some work in the client

sync/async → we want to do some sync work and some async work

build/runtime → we want to do some work at build time and some work at runtime

static/dynamic → we want to some static and dynamic code analysis

preload-prerender/defer load-defer render → we want to preload code and data before we need it, but we want to defer code and data until we need it.

wip/done → we need wip to move forward, but we need to finish the wip to move forward

---

# Do not answer Twice

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/do-not-answer-twice
Tags: writing, scaling, seo

I have a principles that it is called "Do not answer twice"

The idea is that I don't want to answer the same question more than once.

This sounds like a crazy optimization idea, but in my scale it is needed.

After I've founded React community in Brazil, and start answering many questions every day.
Then, I realize that most of the questions will repeat themselves once in a while, like a cycle.

I decide to stop answer questions in private, and asking people to ask their questions in public on Twitter and tag me.
I did a retweet of their questions, and answered them in public.

So, you someone else asks the same question, I just reuse my answer.

I write answers as tweets, tweet threads, blog posts, articles, and here in my zettelkasten.

# Editor - React Conf

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/editor-react-conf
Tags: frontend, react

Content Editable is an attribute that let any element to be editable

Content Editable is usually use to build rich text editors, or markdown editors, or any kind of editors.

[The era of Content Builders](./the-era-of-content-builders)

- https://medium.engineering/why-contenteditable-is-terrible-122d8a40e480

**What you need for a Editor?**

You need a model for the document

You need a map 1-1 from document to visible screen (usually DOM or native nodes)

You need to handle selections in a good way

You need to handle carets

You need to define edit operations based on key press and mouse clicks

**How Medium editor works?**

- it has sections and paragraphs
- a paragraph contains text and formatting, and also a layout information
- a section describes background for a sublist of paragraphs

**How Notion editor works?**

it has a list of basic blocks (text, page, todo list, image, kanban, calendar, database)

each basic block has its own properties

You edit one block per time.

React Conf BR

Drafjs: from RichText to Content Builders

- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rHat0n1xBVc

- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w-PqnpMizcQ

- https://learn-draftjs-now.vercel.app/data-model

# Effective Twitter

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/effective-twitter
Tags: twitter, writing, audience

If you still have a twitter account you can use it to build and grow your audience

The audience is the people that followed you based on the content you create everyday.

The bigger your audience the bigger your reach.

You can use the audience for many reasons, make it easy to find good people to hire to your company, to sell products or courses, spread your ideas.

@jabur

funis de vendas e contratação

funnel top

Time

When you post influences how many people are wake, and how many will interact/engage with your tweet

Prefer 8am to 8pm of your audience timezone. I try to overlap Brazil and US timezone.

Content

A Tweet with just a text provided fewer context and could not be understand well by everybody.

Adding images, gifs, video could improve engagement of your tweets

Links with social media preview also improve engagement

Threads helps you to provide info that won’t fit in a single tweet, or a list of things you wanna share.

It could also be a short blog.

Tagging account could also increase reach if the people tagged has a lot of followers.

Sharing

Only posting on twitter could not be enough, try to post in other communities: slack, discord, Facebook groups, WhatsApp groups, telegram and so on.

Also send to friends, and ask for retweets to improve reach

Send it to friends, and ask for retweets to improve your reach.

Remember, only posting on Twitter could not be enough, try to post in other communities: slack, discord, Facebook groups, WhatsApp groups, telegram, and so on.

morry - improve

Audience and consistency

Tweeting about other topics not related to the audience you wanna reach could give you some unfollows, like tweeting about politics.

However, I don’t care about this, as I am not only a tech content creator.

# Entropy

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/entropy
Tags: programming, code-quality

Code entropy

adding a new prop to your react component increases entropy

adding a new parameter to your funciton increases entropy

more code more entropy

more parameters more entropy

more customization more entropy

Broken windows

Slow code

Half refactors

Wrong abstraction will make it hard to do simple and common things

# ETH

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/eth
Tags: crypto, blockchain

Ethereum is like Bitcoin but with turing complete smart contracts

ECR-20 token

tokens only exist inside a contract

0eth to transfer token + gas fee

ecr-20 complaint - fungible (same value for each token, like money)

totalSupply, balanceOf, transfer, transferFrom, approve, and allowance. In addition, you can specify optional functions, such as name, symbol, and decimal

liquidity pool - unisawp - x \* y = k (k constant, total liquidity)

eth ↔ erc-20 token

erc-20 ↔ erc-20 token

ERC-721 non fungible token - each token has a different value - property

erc-721 + erc-165 interface

erc - ethereum request for comment

proof of work - more energy wins

proof of stake - you stake (put some eth money), you someone is randomly assign to validate the block, if you cheat you loose your stack

Practical

- https://cyprianaarons.hashnode.dev/how-to-create-an-nft-on-ethereum-blockchain-ckp8r1wzy077104s184ungppu

- https://dev.to/dabit3/the-complete-guide-to-full-stack-ethereum-development-3j13

# Excel

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/excel
Tags: tools, productivity

Excel is a software to process spreadsheet/tabular data

Excel can be think as one of the first [Thinking Tools](./thinking-tools).

You put a lot of number, and start building thinks on top of it, using formulas per cell or Visual Basic Scripts.

The basic building block ([Where good ideas come from](./where-good-ideas-come-from) , [The era of Content Builders](./the-era-of-content-builders) ) is the cell.

A cell can contain a basic type (string, number, currency, date)

A cell can contain formatting (background color, color, font-size and more)

You can span a cell to contain more than one column

You can use Excel to import ([Importing data using csv / xlsx](./importing-data-using-csv-xlsx) ) or export data.

Airtable is the new "Excel". Acts likes a spreadsheet but gives you the power of a database

You can see the same data in different ways in Airtable: Calendar, Grid, Kanban, Gallery, Form

# frontend hiring questions

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/frontend-hiring-questions
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## frontend questions

"Good backend hiring question?"

- how to scale frontend? a good answer is to use a design system
- how to scale css? use design system
- What do you test on the frontend? integration test, test the behavior, using testing library, test that when filling out a form and clicking the submit button, the api is called with the correct data
- how do you create a new page? does it start with a component and then break it down (top down), or does it start with base components and then compose them? a good answer would be to use top-down, because segmenting (componentizing) is very difficult if you don't know how it will be structured, another good answer is to use only the components that already exist in the design system
- if a component doesn't exist in the design system for a page you need to do what do you do? A good answer would be to discuss with the designer whether to use an existing component or add the new component to the design system.
- what is the tradeoff of adding a new component to a design system? the more components, the more complexity and work to maintain, the fewer simpler components
- how to organize a design system? A good answer is to have documentation, using docusuarus and/or storybook
- how do you deal with data fetching? The best answer would be relay, but it only works if you have graphql, another answer would be something more level and declarative like react-query, data fetching by hand is always an error
- create a new component or a new prop? prefer a prop if the "new behavior" converges with the existing component, otherwise create a new component
- how to start a new design system? decide the initial basic components, typography, scaping, buttons
- what is important is a design system? consistency, maintainability, scalability, typography, basic components, storybook, documentation
- when to use SSR? when you need perf and SEO, SSR is to render the frontend in the server and hydrate
- what is hydration? it is the process of conciliating the server rendered html with the client rendered html
- how to improve SEO? use SSR, use meta tags, use structured data, use sitemap, use robots.txt, make site fast
- how to improve frontend performance? lazy loading, RSC, SSR, tree shaking, remove big packages
- when to virtualize a list? when we are handling big number of items
- when to memo a component? when you need to render a lot of number of this components
- how to manage state? prefer local state using useState, only when needed use useContext, move data fetching to something else like relay, react-query
- how to build complex forms with validations ? prefer use packages like formik and yup
- how to deploy frontend ? you can deploy on s3 and expose then using nginx, cloudfront or cloudflare pages, any CDN works.

# Functional Programming

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/functional-programming
Tags: programming

The building block of functional programming is a function

A function is an abstraction that receives an input and produces an output

f(x) ⇒ y

A pure function is a function that returns the same return for the same input.

Pure functions are easy to test as you don’t have to mock external parts and there is no side effects.

You can functional programs composing functions.

Types define which values are valid for a given variables or function argument or return.

We can only compose functions that one

# Git branching

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/git-branching
Tags: git, development

People usually stick with the first solution or approach they find to solve their problem. Best practice is think as the silver bullet for a problem without even thinking about it. When you pick a best practice without thinking you are outsourcing all the decisions and choices to the own who created the best practice. It could be the wrong tradeoffs for your problem.

Why do we use git for software development? We need a way to distribute/decentralize the development of the software without one developer causing issues to another one. After the code was made in isolation, we need to integrate it in the main repository. This is usually made using pull requests.

Pull requests enable you request reviews/feedbacks of your code before adding in the main branch. It also let you discover if your approach break any existing behavior or tests

the size of pull requests matters a lot. Small pull requests are easy and faster to review and have less risky of introductions bugs or regressions.

What is wrong about git flow? What is wrong about develop branch?

[https://www.atlassian.com/continuous-delivery/continuous-integration/trunk-based-development](https://www.atlassian.com/continuous-delivery/continuous-integration/trunk-based-development)

# Global State

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/global-state
Tags: react, frontend, relay

#react #global #state

Redux

single immutable atom for the whole UI

hard to code split

hard to optimize

Selector: useSelector

Recoiljs

multiple immutable atoms for the UI

it works with sync and async data

it has support to derived data

optimized to avoid re-rendering parts that don't consume an atom

getters vs setters

Selector: useRecoilValue

Context

React context can only has one single value, so you need to use subscribe pattern to avoid re-rendering all components that consume them

Selector: useContext

Relay

Single store

Selector: GraphQL fragments

Mobx

Observables

Semi Global

Formik:

form field state should be able to be validated together

one form field change should not re-render all other fields, so it has good perf

They keep me asking "simple" questions.

Struggle help them to learn better and to improve their understanding of what they are learning.

# how to contribute to open source

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/how-to-contribute-to-open-source
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## how to contribute to open source?

"Are there specific projects or types of open source contributions that you would recommend to someone in my current career (internship)?"

You can contribute to any open source project.
If you say you can't, it is a barrier that you created.

I would recommend contribute and be comfortable with open source.

First, watch the repo that you want to contribute.
Start contributing answers all open issues.
Also do code review of all open pull requests.
Read all the code and documentation to see if you can contribute with some easy stuff first.
As you go, you can contribute.

You only be able to contribute meaninfully for packages/libraries/projects that you use.
If you don't use a project you can't contribute, because you don't know what is good or bad, or what is missing.
You need to use the project and feel the pain.
After that it will be easy to see what is missing, and you can have some idea of how to contribute.

# How to deal with customers in a SH

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/how-to-deal-with-customers-in-a-sh
Tags: software-house, customers

A software house build customized software for other companies.

Most software house do everything that a customer ask them for, this sounds like the only way to do business as you are paying for that.

What if I told you that you don't need to do everything your customer ask your for?

The idea is that if you accept every single feature or request from your customer you will make things hard and harder for you in the long term.

Customer usually don't know what they really want, when you receive a new feature request for them.

Ask to yourself what is the real problem that he/she is trying to solve?

Can we solve in a simpler way? Can we avoid this?

# How to find the best solution?

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/how-to-find-the-best-solution
Tags: problem-solving, software

Your first solution for a problem won’t be the best one.

The first thing you need to do when trying to solve a problem is to research for existing solutions for the given problem. Most of the time someone else already solved your problem or a similar one. After having a list of possible solutions you should evaluate them using some criteria.

A problem always has more than one solution. Finding the best solution is an optimization problem where you use some criteria to evaluate the score of your solution.

You can have some requirements that you should meet eliminating a few possible solutions. After finding the minimal set of possible solutions you need to try all of them in small proof of concepts to understanding their tradeoffs in practice. The simplest solution should be preferred.

If you want to use this solution in a production system with a team, you have some more steps to follow. You need to ensure you can deliver this solution incrementally without breaking anything. You also need to write a RFC and demo your solution to your team, to make sure everybody is onboard. Other people can find problems in your proposed solution and edge cases that you have not thought about it, making you need to reevaluate your approach.

Summary

Finding the best solution for a given problem takes sometime as you need to evaluate many options before deciding. Picking the first one or the “best practice” or most used solution could not be the best solution for your problem and requirements.

Team members can invalidate your proposed solution and help you reach a better solution. Adding a solution for a production running system can be more challenge and require tweaks

---

Feedbacks

Quasar

- Your first solution for a problem \[probably\] won’t be the best one, it happens, rarely but happens
- You can also use a provisional solution depending on your context/time/urgency as long as there is the possibility of an incremental update
- Talk about different solutions in the same testing system and bold the importance of a good test set - actual good tests can cover actions regardless of your internal methods, if your solution is clear it will have a pattern that can be resolved by any change

1. Can you explain your solution clearly?
2. Can your solution be tested?
3. Will small changes in your solution break the tests?
4. Can you upgrade your solution?

Pedro

Carolis

I think the sentences citing "criteria" are a little repetitive, mainly because they are very close in the text structure

# how to prioritize learning

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/how-to-prioritize-learning
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## how to prioritize learning

"How can I identify and prioritize which technologies or programming languages to learn given long-term career goals?"

Learn what will help you achieve your goals first.

If you want to get your first job, learn the tech stack that most companies are loooking for.

If they are looking for Go, you learn Go.
You learn Go and show that you can build using Go what they are needing.
That you can build a CRUD API with Go, that you can implement event driven with Go.
That you can create automation using Go.
Study the company, the products, the problems they are facing.
And how can you solve it using the tech stack that they use.

You need to balance with topics that you need right now.
For instance, we need to improve a lot our DevOps workflow, so I spend a lot of time studying and testing a lot of DevOps workflows.
I also studied things that I won't use on DevOps right now, but can be useful in the future.

## how to stand out

The ones that make things cheaper, faster stands out

The ones that work in the hardest and more complex projects stands out

The ones that create new things stands out

The ones that make the company make more money, bring more customers stands out

# How to Take Smart Notes

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/how-to-take-smart-notes
Tags: zettelkasten, writing, books

#note #organization

Successful writing comes from good note taking

- https://www.amazon.co.uk/How-Take-Smart-Notes-Nonfiction-ebook/dp/B06WVYW33Y/ref=as_li_ss_tl?ie=UTF8&linkCode=sl1&tag=brykam-21&linkId=1b678d6bc3d383a145517578e8abb559&language=en_GB

> “Getting something that is already written into another written piece is incomparably easier than assembling everything in your mind and then trying to retrieve it from there.”

You need the [Habit](./habit) of note taking to write well

> “Having a meaningful and well-defined task beats willpower every time.”

> “Routines require simple, repeatable tasks that can become automatic and fit together seamlessly”

the new routine will feel artificial at first, much like an habit change

This method is similar to [Getting Things Done](./getting-things-done)

1. fleeting notes: capture everything that come up in your mind
2. literature notes: notes about something that you read
3. permanent notes: bring notes from 1/2 and add more metadata, links them, improve them.

You invert the process of writing. You first read a lot of content that you are interested in.

Then when you have many content about some ideas/concepts, you can organized the pieces and write about it

you need serendipity to find new ideas

In which context do you want to find this note?

> “Making something public always means to write it down so it can be read.”

Go in public to gather feedback of your thoughts/ideas

An expert acts on intuition because all the rules and knowledge are internalized. They don't need conscious to act properly.

An expert can see patterns that begineers can't

Things we understand are connected, it is easier to remember interconnected things, like the slip-box

# Human Computation

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/human-computation
Tags: computing, crowdsourcing

Human Computation is when you use Humans to perform tasks that humans are better can machine. It is like humans helping computers.

Luis Von Ahn made a lot of programs and games to use human base computation to solve problems where machine is not so goof.

Duolingo knows that the best translators are humans. It sends real text to advanced learners train that are piece of websites, they translated buzzfeed using this strategy.

Google images first version was a game where 2 users without communicate needs to say what is inside an image. After discovering some things inside the image these words become taboo to find more objects and things.

The second version of this game was used to segment images, given a word one user would show part of the image to the other player show tell what you as it.

It also made ReCaptcha where users tell the numbers inside images to handle ocr/ digits recognization.

# Human Search Engine

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/human-search-engine
Tags: search, zettelkasten, writing

#substack

This is the preparation for Search Engine blogpost on [Substack](./substack)

it will be built on top of [Search](./search) , [Index](./index-note) and Zettelkasten ideas

---

Outline

- What is search?
- Why we need search?
- Why bookmark, tags are not enough?
- How can we build our own search index
- How to incrementally tweak and improve your search index
- Practical index building

After using Google for many years we think search is a synonymous of Google.

Google is really good to help us find information, websites, places, content, news, products, flights and many more information.

**What is search?**

Search is how we find information.

We use google in a daily basis to find websites, places, products, flights.

To perform search we provide a text query usually a question, some keywords, and hope we find the information we needed.

Mac Spotlight let us find "anything" in our desktop. It can find documents, applications and more.

Some apps has a spotlight search approach, in notion you can find pages and more.

Webstorm let you search for filenames, variables, functions, classes, components and more.

**Why we need search?**

Our minds are powerful but limited, we can't retrieve most of information from our minds.

**How can we build our own search index?**

Have you ever forget about something: a book, a movie, a link, a github repo?

This happen for a number of reasons

We haven't written down about the book

We haven't add some metadata or text to help us find this books later one

We haven't linked this book to other books we had read

**Why bookmarks does not work?**

If you keep a list of bookmarks in your browser you can't add metadata to them

You can't easily search them, you need to open them to figure it out what it was about

You can't link one link to another.

**Why folders does not work?**

Categories and subcategories will overlap somewhere, and you're gonna have the paradox of where to put the things you wanna remember.

**How to incrementally build and improve index?**

Every time you hit a miss (try to find something but it won't get it easy).

Add a new note (zettel) to your note taking (zetteltask). I'm using notion for my note taking.

Add the link/idea/book/website/movie/podcast in the note

Add text that would make you find it later in an easy way. What were the keywords that you used to find it this time?

Add labels/tags to add them to some categories

Link this note to other related notes, so you can find it following a web of connections.

Let's see how I index some common things

Book

When reading a book, I create a new entry for it.

A write down with my own words core ideas of the book.

I create 1 new entry for each core idea, so I can link them to other books and sources.

I quote some passages of it (very few ones)

A link the book to other related books and sources.

Person

I write down a short description to identify the person

I can have a small picture to make remembering easier

I write down some ideas that person has

The job of this person

contact information

link this person to books, and other people

Make your search [Future Proof](./future-proof) always testing them

- https://www.swyx.io/writing/keyboard-first

Find everything just typing.

We can use [Human Computation](./human-computation) to improve our search engine

You need to provide the right cues to remember

An index is A systematically way to provide cues

You usually search by prefix postfix

You usualy search by keywords

You usualy search by related notes/ideas

You usually search by synonymous

how do index videos/podcasts?

When watching a video/podcast I write down some draft/raw notes based on concepts of it.

Then when the video/podcast is over, I reread then and compile them with only the essential parts.

Feedback

A única parte que precisei reler mais foi "A note will be the building block for our index." porque não foi tão claro o conceito de building blocks pra mim. Não ficaria melhor colocar "A note will be the documento for our index"? Porque na figura acima você usou "Documents" na segunda coluna

# Importing data using csv / xlsx

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/importing-data-using-csv-xlsx
Tags: software, data

#blog #substack #twitter

What can go wrong when importing data using .csv or .xlsx files?

**Dates/Times**

csv/xlsx files does not ensure the user will use the data formatting that you asked them for.

You can use the date format in xlsx, but user can modify the column to remove this formatting, or pasting the wrong date format altogether.

You can also handle dates as string or let your xlsx parser to try to parse to you.

The most common problem is that some countries using dd/mm/yyyy and other uses mm/dd/yyyy. You can use some Heuristic to try to correct parse them, as some dates only works in a given format. You could also use the date format of the locale of the user, but it won't tell much about the language of the file the user used to edit the import data.

You also need to handle timezone possible issues as always.

**Header/Columns**

Users can modify the header of your import file, so your importing strategy will fail.

You could enforce the column number, but users will change this order

You could enforce the column header label, but users will change them

You could try to match them using a Heuristic that this will also fail

You can let user tells you what is inside each column

**Booleans**

You can predefined a set of strings to represent truth and false values

It can be in english and also in the language of your users.

You should also lowercase them to make comparison more stable, as users can behave and act differently.

**Conditional Fields**

One column/field can affect other field.

One field can make another field required

One field can be exclusive against other (you can't have both)

**Validations**

Each column can have a data type (string, number, date, ID, boolean and more).

Your validations can be global or local

If you are importing users, you need a global validation to make sure they does not have conflicts primary keys.

You need local validation per row, to make sure all required columns are defined.

You also need to make sure all columns have the proper type.

If you have an ID reference to some database data, you need to make sure the ID is valid, and it is stored in the database.

**Error Handling**

Instead of a stack trace, we need to provide a file trace of error that happened during the processing.

We can have 3 types of errors: global, per row, or per column.

Global: it happens when 2 or more rows conflicts

Per row: it happens when all columns are valid individually but an error happen when they are used together.

Per column: it happens when a given column is wrong, and break the processing of a given row.

**Space**

We can have space before and after data because user typed spaced without noticing.

We should trim any data before processing it.

**Showing Results**

You need to show what rows were imported successfully.

You also need to who which rows were not processed correctly and why.

# In Conclusion

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/in-conclusion
Tags: writing

1. **To Summarize**: Succinctly recap the main points discussed throughout the article.
2. **In Summary**: Provide a brief and concise recap of the article's content.
3. **To Conclude**: Offer a closing thought or statement summarizing the key ideas.
4. **Wrapping Up**: Signal that the article is concluding and summarize the main takeaways.
5. **Final Thoughts**: Share your final reflections, insights, or opinions on the topic.
6. **Closing Remarks**: Add some concluding comments, impressions, or opinions.
7. **To Wrap It Up**: Summarize the article's main points and bring the discussion to a close.
8. **Last Words**: Offer some final insights or thoughts on the subject matter.
9. **The Takeaway**: Highlight the central message or primary lessons for the reader.
10. **In Closing**: Provide a concise summary and any last considerations.
11. **To End**: Convey that the article is nearing its conclusion and offer a summary.
12. **To Sum Up**: Recap the article's key points in a clear and concise manner.
13. **In Summary of All This**: Summarize the article's main points and tie them together.
14. **To Recap**: Offer a brief overview of the main discussion points.
15. **To Close**: Signal the article's conclusion and summarize the essential content.

# Index

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/index-note
Tags: search, zettelkasten

#index #retrieving

Indexing is the art of making retrieving data faster

Elastic Search (lucene) uses an inverted index to retrieve all documents fast.

An inverted index is like this:

doc1 - Awesome

doc2: Alert

doc3: Beta

doc4: Crud

doc4: Create

A - doc1, doc2

B - doc3

C - doc4, doc5

It search based on prefix/suffix to reduce the search time

Zettelkasten is like an index for our brain, as we can find ideas/thoughts faster than using another method

we can search using tags, full text search and links among notes

# Issue

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/issue
Tags: project-management, development

#issue #project #management

Issue is an [Atom](./atom) task.

It represent a chunk of work to produce something

It can represent a new feature that needs to be implemented

It can represent a bug that needs to be solved

It can represent an improvement

It can represent a technical debt that needs to be solved

You can add labels to issues (metadata) to making them easier to find, and also group them

You can also link other issues, pull requests, commits to add more context to the issue.

You can attach an issue to a temporal context using a milestone

A milestone represent a list of issues that should be worked in a given space of time

# knowledge value

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/knowledge-value
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## knowledge value

"How I can calculate values of my knowlege? Example: My cost about work far away from home is R$2.866,80/month.
But I learning a lot that put in balance is worth. Exists a away to calculate this?"

Knowledge does not have an intrisic value.
The value of knowledge is related to their scarcity and demand.

If you know something that a lot of people and companies need, and a few people know it, you can charge a lot for it.

If you think you are not earning as much as you should, you should try to ask for a raise, or switch jobs.

Let the market decide how much your knowledge is worth.
The more worth the easier is to get a raise or switch jobs.

# Layers

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/layers
Tags: computer-science, learning

After Tobi talking about there is not such thing as frontend engineer and that you need to know more layers

I'd like to talk about all the layers that I've learning in college

Some people think that college is a waste of money and time for computer science.

I think if you can afford it, you should do it.

It will give you all the base that you gonna need to solve any kind of problem that come up to you.

I think we can go from electrons to no-code to cover all layers and abstractions that you need to know, not master, to understand what it is really going on.

The basic building blocks of a CPU is the transistor.

A transistor let electric current pass given a following configuration.

So we have 0 and 1, binary. 0 is no current and 1 is current.

And everything is built on top of this concept.

Then we have boolean logic, that let us sum, subtract and to most math using binary code.

We use logic ports to create basic arithmetic.

If you add PC (program counter), a clock, you have a basic CPU.

If you can load data from memory and write to memory, you can do anything your modern computer does.

You can build your own assembly, then you decode each instructions and execute simple programs.

After that you could keep using assembly, or build a higher level language to compile to assembly to make your life easier, like C.

# leadership migration

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/leadership-migration
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## leadership migration

"What strategies do you recommend for effectively transitioning into technology leadership roles?"

The most effective strategy is to start leading right now in your current role.

YOu also need to be in an organization that needs more leadership

You should be leading your team, your product, your feature before even being assigned to this role.

Performing the activities of the leader before being a leader is the best way to be promoted to it.

You also need to study a lot about leadership, not only in tech but the social part.
Read a lot of content about it.

Deliver results with high quality will give you trust to be promoted to a leader

Also make it clear that you want to be a leader

can I use gatsby image outside gatsby?

can I use apollo cache outside apollo server?

# Learning a new language

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/learning-a-new-language
Tags: learning, language

#learning #language

When I'm learning a new language I try to immerse myself with the language.

I've change my computer, mobile phone, browser and everything to the related language.

I'm using duolingo to learn spanish, I'm not spending many time per day learning spanish, but I'm learning some everyday.

I think consistency is better in the long run.

Learning a new language needs time, as learning everything else

I always try to think in the new language, and if I don't know how to say something in it, I use google translate to help me out.

I also to some dumb stuff as mixing my talk and writing with the new language, so you gonna see me trying to use the new language in my life with my wife and kid when thought they don't understand much about it.

Spanish is "harder" because it is to close to Portuguese, so most people think they don't need to learn it, but it has a lot of nuances.

Languages has also a lot of details that you learn as you use more and more.

We have false cognates that are words that you write in a similar way but means something completely different, so you need to unlearn and let your brain relearn again

\## Links

[Make it stick](./make-it-stick)

# learning depth or breadth

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/learning-depth-or-breadth
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## learning depth or breadth ?

"How can I effectively balance the desire to learn new technologies with the need to deepen my knowledge of the ones I am already studying?"

My advice here is to focus more on solving problems.
And solving a new problem usually is a combination of solving some existing problem that you already solved,
some problems that you don't know how to solve, and some knowledge and experience that you have and some that you are missing.

Most of the time you should focus on breadth if you want to solve more kind of problems.
You focus in learning few about a lot of things.

If you want to solve better a kind of problem you need to go in depth.
You focus in learning a lot about a few things.

You need to balance these approaches.

I usually only go deep when my current knowldge/experience is not enough to solve the problem that I have to solve.

---

# Learning Path AWS Lambda

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/learning-path/learning-path-aws-lambda
Tags: learning-path, aws, lambda, backend

- [ ] learn how to bundle backend using webpack in a single bundle (check this https://gist.github.com/jgcmarins/2860f547f5d785dce24ca0eadbe3abdd)
- [ ] learn how to automate lamdba deploys using serveless or aws cdk (github actions)
- [ ] learn how to configure and automate api gateway
- [ ] learn how to automate tests lambdas using jest
- [ ] learn how to configure, automate and use RDS Proxy to fast database workflow in lamdbas (also cache database connections)
- [ ] how the performance gain using RDS Proxy over normal database usage
- [ ] learn about cold start and lambda statefull (https://www.swyx.io/stateful-serverless/)
- [ ] expose a CRUD api in lamdba
- [ ] put everything on open source (github)
- [ ] write a blog post about each of the topics above
- [ ] deploy in your AWS account

- [ ] learn how to test your API using Postman, and also automated using jest and supertest

- [ ] Introduction to serverless computing and its benefits

## learning structure

"How can I structure my learning to cover both the fundamental bases and emerging technologies in programming?"

Focus on concepts

Structure as a roadmap - things that you need to learn, and things that you need to build

Check my [Learning Paths](https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/category/learning-path)

You need to learn the theory, but you need to build to get the practice, and understand how really works

the new tech is just an implementation detail of existing concepts

# Links

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/links
Tags: zettelkasten, web

&lt;a/>

href

Links are how we link one content/idea to another

Links are the base of internet/web

Links are the base for Zettelkasten

You can link another website, you can “link” a channel, you can link a Person, you can link a page

Links representa references

Links are the evolution of references, as you just need to click to know more

Link more

You link collections using joins or lookups

The web of life good shows that isolated parts does not contains the properties of the whole

The links bring second order effects to the web

We use graphs and edges/links among nodes to represent relationship, like follow unfollow or friendship

We can have unidirectional links or bidirectional links

As we see in PageRank every node is connected even by a small probability

We can use links to show a list of related things

Related projects on github

Related books

# Looking for the First Job

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/looking-for-the-first-job
Tags: job, hiring, hack

[Versão em Português](https://gist.github.com/sermoud/b30a36058cdad95d4a048740307b8e71)

This is a very common state for people in college, people before/after a bootcamp, or people from another area.

The first job will be the hardest one to get, but it will get easier over time.

The interview will be harder than the job itself

After knowing a bit of programming, you need to practice a lot (like many hours, 10k hours) to get really good at it.

read the book outliers about it (10k rule). gap

<Embed url='https://twitter.com/sseraphini/status/1376509751861854214' />

I do recommend building open source projects with the stack you want to learn and improve. I recommend fullstack javascript

If you get stuck you can ask for help on twitter/slack/discord communities and tag me.

asking questions (even "dumb" ones) will help you process

ask in public ([https://www.swyx.io/learn-in-public/](https://www.swyx.io/learn-in-public/)) so more people can learn from the same questions, and you can break your fear of showing that you don't know something

I don't know a lot of stuff, the first thing is learning that you don't know something, and trying to figure it out how to learn that after all.

You should apply to as many job posting as possible.

Do all the code challenges to learn what the companies want you to know, you gonna learn a lot coding them.

Do as many interviews so you can get good at interviews.

All this practice will get you a job soon or later. it can take some time, you just need to persist.

Always ask for feedback for the code challenges and interview, listening to feedback is the only way to improve and learn.

There are many ways to learn something, so consume content in a variety of medium (text, video, audio, code), but also make sure that you are not passive learning.

You need to be active and build stuff using something that you are reading/watching about it.

[Advice for developers](./advice-for-developers)
