Apply concepts in real life to make them stick

Exercise/tests can help you

Tests yourself knowledge to stop forgetting

To learn more stop forgetting

interleave content learning

learning that takes effort stay deeper in your mind

Learn and practice in a multitude of ways, variation is important to learn and be robust to transfer learn to other situations

machine learning apply a lot of them

it separates training from tests

it learns from many different types of examples to learn similarities and divergences

**substack**

You can learn anything.

I’m a self-learning since very early in my life (12 years old), not everyone try to optimize their learning process.

# Mappers vs Packers

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/mappers-vs-packers
Tags: learning, mental-models

- https://www.reciprocality.org/Reciprocality/r0/index.html
- https://www.datapacrat.com/Opinion/Reciprocality/r0/Day1.html
- https://datapacrat.com/Opinion/Reciprocality/r0/index.html

“knowledge packets” - little bits of truth (or errors) that we possess.

most learning are almost entirely on the acquisition of knowledge packets

things that one should or should not do.

data to be retained and later recovered on demand

we don't just stack up knowledge packets

to gain each new knowledge packet we ask “why”

a mental map gives us understanding of cause and effect within a situation.

this understanding allow us to derive a solution to any problem within the situation, instead of attempting to select a rote-learned response.

mathematicians call “isomorphism”, machine learning calls “invariance”, where you can reapply knowledge

we rearrange our mental maps to product simpler expressions, we find it hard when the topic seemed complicated

abstract pattern recognition

without reflections, there can be no mental maps, only knowledge packets.

reflection is daydreaming

packing is when you stop youself asking “why”

rote-learned memory - memória aprendida

rote-learned response - resposta memorizada

you try to find a knowledge packet that fits your situation.

without a big map means that you often don't understand what is happening

packers are overly concerned about certainty. they don't want to fix their mental model, they wanna validate that their mental model is correct.

people are unwilling to think about something unless they are “certain”

you fear of being found to be in the wrong

they cannot believe that anything can be achieved unless someone else spells out in exact detail how to do absolutely everything

---

# maximize impact in large organizations

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/maximize-impact-in-large-organizations
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## maximize impact in large organizations

"How can I maximize the impact of my projects in large organizations?"

Find team/products/features/projects that will maximize the impact inside your large organization

if you are not in the best team, working in the hardest problems of your large organization.
Your effort will be limited to your team impact.

After finding the hardest problems of your organization and joining the team/squad that work on it.
You should show that you can deliver the solutions for these problems with quality.
You need to earn trust, and bring your ideas over RFC and win the team.

You need to deeply understand the company business, products to understand what needs to be done to make your company succeed.

# Memory Leak

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/memory-leak
Tags: nodejs, testing

```
node --expose-gc ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand --logHeapUsage packages/main/src/modules/auth/admin/mutations/__tests__
```

```
node --inspect-brk --expose-gc ./node_modules/.bin/jest --runInBand --logHeapUsage packages/main/src/modules/auth/admin/mutations/__tests__
```

- https://chanind.github.io/javascript/2019/10/12/jest-tests-memory-leak.html

Memory leak when you allocated some memory and didn't dispose it.

# Mongodb

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/mongodb
Tags: database, mongodb

Mongodb is a nosql database that bring a lot of innovation in the javascript ecosystem

Mongo let us do complex queries using aggregation framework

We can use $lookup to join 2 collections, or many other operations as we need

Mongo is great because it is close to javascript to do queries and updates.

compound indexes

- https://emptysqua.re/blog/optimizing-mongodb-compound-indexes/

- http://www.askasya.com/

To speed up your queries move most of index filtering processing to the top

- https://amyportela.github.io/posts/mongodb_index_explain.html

# Newsletters

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/newsletters
Tags: writing, newsletter

#newsletter #writing

Newsletters have a different incentive than normal blog posts

When you do a blog post, one post is not related to another.

The likes from one blog post won't affect another one.

When you are building a newsletters, the incentive is to keep producing content in a regular basis to grow your audience (subscribers)

Improve [First Impression](./first-impression)

# NoCode

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/nocode
Tags: nocode, programming

NoCode is building software using "code" (pure text).

It is a higher level way to build software.

You can build software using pre built building blocks ([The era of Content Builders](./the-era-of-content-builders) ).

You can drag and drop blocks and see they running

They follow WYSIWYG (what you see is what you get).

We have a variety of nocode to build websites: WebFlow, Wix, Canva

For backend the options are more limited: DarkLang

- https://darklang.com/

One benefit if that you don't have the deploy flow anymore, everything will do is deploied already. You just need to move from dev to staging to production.

The feedback loop is much faster.

One drawback is that people without coding background will build back data layers, making the nocode application not scale well.

We can think of nocode as another [Thinking Tools](./thinking-tools), as we can build fast prototipes, and then just join the pieces to build it up.

What is missing to NoCode catch up?

Usually you can't compose nocode?

Can you build a design system in nocode?

How do we share nocode ?

Do we need a package manager for nocode?

Incremental approach for you nocode

---

# Node Modules

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/node-modules
Tags: nodejs, npm

#node #npm #packages

node\_modules is where node keeps all their dependencies

one good thing of node\_modules is that you can easily modify an external package code inside node\_modules and test your fix before sending a pull request

node\_modules also applies the colocation pattern, where the dependencies are close to the project

If you check C,C++,python,ruby, GO and other, the deps are not close to where there are used. So it is much harder to modify deps and contribute back

if you use monorepo with yarn workspaces you gonna have many node\_modules. One at the root and one at each package level. Yarn will hoist same package version range to the node\_modules in the root.

Hoist caused many problems as most tool have the wrong assumptions that node\_modules is besides the package, and also the package

if your node\_modules is big it is be slow to load packages, as node tranverse the node\_modules to find it

reduce node modules techniques

- https://tsh.io/blog/reduce-node-modules-for-better-performance/

- use `-production` flag
- node-prune / modclean

https://gist.github.com/greim/e8e1bd3b1ed08a7505ce

- move deps to devDepencies
- improve .npmignore

only pick select fields on package.json

- https://github.com/n1ru4l/use-async-effect/blob/7da6f9915832d63abcf6c93775e8dcbdd70f0cb6/scripts/prepare-deploy-package-json.js

```javascript
const pickFields = [
  'name',
  'version',
  'license',
  'author',
  'homepage',
  'repository',
  'bugs',
  'keywords',
  'module',
  'main',
  'typings',
  'dependencies',
  'peerDependencies',
  'files',
];
```

# O(1) - Constant Time

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/o-1-constant-time
Tags: productivity, learning

How can you solve anything fast? At a constant time?

Everything that you solved before becomes 0(1) to solve again

It basically says that any solution that you come up before should make it straight forward to implement again.

To be [Productivity](./productivity) , you need to be unproductive for many hours.

# Open Source

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/open-source
Tags: opensource, community

#community #opensource #code

Open Source is when you share you code in the public to be consumed to somebody else

My history with open source started when I was working in an android app to track sensors information to build a machine learning model

my contribution was inside an issue instead of a pull request

At that time I didn't understand much about git, git workflows, branches and so on and so forth

When I started working on PontoTel I contribute to some angular packages in a more mainstream way.

When starting working in react native (very early, lots of stuff to build), I contribute much more as I just needed to change some code inside node\_modules and send a pull request based on my forks.

I've opened a lot of issues in many repos showing all the "bugs", "problems" and "limitations" that I've found when development Brand Lovers.

We did revamp the react-native-camera based on expo-camera because we needed to do facial recognition on Gol app and rctcamera couldn't handle it. We decided to copy and paste the code (giving attribution to expo), because back them expo-camera was too tight to "expo framework". After all this the RNCamera diverged a lot from expo-camera.

I hope someday they will be joined again.

# Page based pagination with Connections

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/page-based-pagination-with-connections
Tags: relay, graphql

There are no public examples of doing paged based pagination with Connection in [Relay](./relay) .

Page based is a very common pattern in business apps, so it should be easy in Relay.

Artsy made some prior work

- https://artsy.github.io/blog/2020/01/21/graphql-relay-windowed-pagination/

but it feels not good to me

- https://andrewingram.net/posts/demystifying-graphql-connections/

We can augment connection arguments to also include limit and offset to enable page based pagination.

We also need to modify Connection Handler (https://github.com/facebook/relay/blob/master/packages/relay-runtime/handlers/RelayDefaultHandlerProvider.js#L25), to make sure the edges are properly added to the right connection

- https://github.com/sibelius/relay-workshop/blob/master/solutions/07-useRefetchableFragment/src/comment/PostComments.tsx#L65

# Paypal mafia

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/paypal-mafia
Tags: startups, culture

http://paulgraham.com/paypal.html

Recognize young people with extraordinary ability

Extreme Focus - everyone should only have #1 initiative

Dedication to individual accomplishment - each innovation were driven by a single person

Refusal to accept constraints, external or internal - if you can't solve a problem, someone else will solve this for you.

Driven problem solvers: smart, driven problem solvers, you just need to be able to solve any problem that appeared

Self-sufficiency: figure it out how to achieve your goals

Extreme bias towards action: you should ship to production

Willingness to try: try new directions often

Data-driven decision making: do your homework, bring your data to support your decisions.

Radical transparency on metrics: share your metrics and let the team extract info

Vigorous debate, often via email: every critical issue needs a champion and critics

Extreme Pressure: be able to work on extreme pressure

# People Recommendation

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/people-recommendation
Tags: career, reputation

Young people does not realize how they are killing their social proof

Why I can't recommend you anymore

I can't recommend you anymore because you lie

You lie that you are going to commit to that company, project, but you just disappear

I can't recommend you because you do not take responsibility for your actions, you blame others instead of saying that you did something wrong.

I can't recommend you because you don't care. You don't care about my friends.

People came to me for recommendations because they know my reputation.

They know I know a lot of good developers because I keep mentoring a lot of them.

They know that I won't recommend a bad developers (not only bad code), but bad matters.

A good reputation can open a lot of good opportunities for you

A bad reputation will close many of them.

# Perishable

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/perishable
Tags: management, startups

We have perishable problems and opportunities

A perishable problem is one that is small at first and can get big fast, so you need to handle it quickly

Example: fire, it is easier to handle small fires.

A perishable opportunity will only be available to the one that grab it first.

Example.: the first company with a covid tracking solution will win the market. The first vaccine will earn a lot of money with roalties

Decentralization can help you solve these perishable problems and to use the opportunities quickly

Escalation can help find important problems

We a mission to align decentralized resources

A mission is a declarative way of the final state

It does not matter what steps or how to achieve this final state

Make intent clear

“If you are going to worry about it, I won’t”

What is our main effort? Main effort of your product? Core features that differentiate from another

# Practical Benefits of an Event Driven Approach

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/practical-benefits-of-an-event-driven-approach
Tags: event-driven, architecture, writing

feedback

Reviewer 1

we can't easily just reprocess `newPayment` without reprocessing the whole `transactionSync`

example of this

if `newPayment` had a bug it won't affect `transactionSync`

you can save events to reprocess then

example of monitoring, apm

---

Reviewer 2

Very good article with interesting content.
Woovi's approach is very like the approach that we are using at another company for payments notifications.

1\. “Three successive sentences begin with the same word”:

> To code newPayment you need to understand how transactionSync works, more cognitive load
> To test newPayment, you need to test transactionSync together, as a consequence you have a more complex test with more complex fixtures and test scenarios.
> To refactor newPayment, you could break transactionSync, these codes are highly coupled.

2\. “This sentence does not start with an uppercase letter”:
To the following phrases:

> we can't easily just reprocess newPayment without reprocessing the whole transactionSync

> we can easily reprocess newPayment without reprocessing the whole transactionSync

---

Reviewer 3

um pequeno typo no texto:

To code newPayment you DON’T need to understand how transactionSync works, fewer cognitive load

---

Reviewer 4

"This article aims to give a real world example and it this clear." -> "This article aims to give a real and clear example."

"The bank sends a new transaction webhook for Woovi backend" -> replace "webhook to Woovi's backend"

---

coproduto

To code newPayment you do need to understand how transactionSync works, fewer cognitive load

acho que era "you do NOT need to understand"

E nesse caso é "less", não "fewer"

Fewer só se usa com coisas contáveis

Tipo, você pode falar "fewer potatoes" mas não "fewer water" (porque batatas são contáveis, mas água não é)

eu consideraria "cognitive load" incontável

Fewer também só se usa em comparações

Você pode considerar que tem uma comparação implícita aí, mas ainda tem o problema da contabilidade

De resto eu curti a ideia do post

Mas eu acho que não ficou muito claro como que isso funcionaria sem usar microsserviços

Eu imagino que você esteja usando um job queue ou algo do tipo?

Talvez fosse bom explicitar como é que esses eventos vão ser processados sem usar serviços

pq do jeito que está parece que você só está jogando um evento pro vácuo e de alguma forma o processamento acontece

Outra coisa também é que não ficou muito claro por que é que as coisas seriam desacopladas

Afinal, você pode escrever a função newPayment de forma desacoplada sem usar eventos também, só tem um ponto de acoplamento necessário entre os dois que é o payload que essa função vai receber

E esse continua, n

né \*

os dois lados têm que concordar com o formato do evento

Então talvez fosse bom explicitar de que tipo de acoplamento você tá falando

# Principles of Product Development Flow

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/principles-of-product-development-flow
Tags: books, product, productivity

#book #product #development #flow

- https://www.amazon.com.br/Principles-Product-Development-Flow-Generation-ebook/dp/B00K7OWG7O/ref=sr_1_1?__mk_pt_BR=%C3%85M%C3%85%C5%BD%C3%95%C3%91&dchild=1&keywords=principles+of+development+flow&qid=1590602126&s=books&sr=1-1

This book is about techniques to improve your product development flow

In manufacturing you generate value creating the same product

In product development you only generate value modifying your existing product

Fullstack handles better variable demand

you can model backend and frontend engineer as processors of queues

If you have variable demands

Sometimes you gonna have much work on backend and sometime more work on frontends

In both scenario you gonna delay your tasks product development

Fullstack acts as a single poll of resources that can handle any item in the queue, causing less delays

Fast refresh is about iteration speed

Integration speed reduces defects

human version of this book

- https://www.amazon.com.br/Phoenix-Project-DevOps-Helping-Business/dp/0988262592?tag=lomadee0850009731-20&ascsubtag=226536112767z176z1590421503440&lmdsid=034436112767-176-1590421503440

# Programing Bottom Up

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/programing-bottom-up
Tags: programming, abstractions

Programing Bottom Up is about creating the low level building blocks improving the language to create your product.

Building Block

# project transitions

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/project-transitions
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## project transitions

"How can I transition from personal projects to more complex or commercial technology projects?"

The only way is to go to production.

You can't learn using only personal projects that do not have outside users/customers.

You need real users to provide feedback to see if your product is good or bad, and if your code is good or bad.

You need a side project with real users, or you need to get freelancers or a real job

At Woovi we are learning a lot everyday because we have more and more users using our product at scale.

# Q&A College

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/qa-college
Tags: qa, college

> As perguntas são muito mais relacionadas à graduação.

> Você acha que o fato de possuir uma graduação na USP te ajudou? Em quais aspectos?

Todo conhecimento acaba te ajudando. Toda a minha base teórica me permite aprender coisas novas mais rapidamente.

> Se você escolhesse não ir para a faculdade, você acha que estaria como?

Minha família é não é rica, acredito que a faculdade me deu confiança e que o diploma da USP me ajudou a conseguir o primeiro emprego.

A faculdade não é só conhecimento. Você faz amigos, você curte as festas, morar sozinho te faz crescer como pessoa, você aprende com a diversidade das pessoas, eu morei na república 7 eh Poko te me ajudou nas minhas social skills. Eu consegui fazer iniciação científica que melhorou meu modo de pensar, eu tive artigos aceitos em conferências e apresente 2 vezes internacionalmente, França e Polônia, tudo pago pela USP. Eu também consegui fazer o ciências sem fronteiras, 1 ano nos USA, que me tornou fluente em inglês e abriu minha cabeca para o mundo.

Se eu tivesse otimizado minha vida no começo para ganhar mais eu saberia menos hoje.

> A experiência de mercado acaba sendo equivalente à uma graduação, ou até melhor?

Conhecimentos distintos, ambos são importantes.

> O que você de hoje falaria para o seu eu de 18 anos, quando estava entrando na faculdade?

Eu tentaria ler mais sobre startups, sobre empreendedorismo. Eu caí no mundo das startups por acaso. Eu comecei a fazer trilha graduação mestrado, fiz 1 semestre fãs matérias de mestrado, meio orientador foi para outro país e eu resolvi aplicar para um estágio de verão na PontoTel. No final eu descobri que as pessoas mais inteligentes do mundo trabalham com negócios e startups.

> Por que optar por fazer uma faculdade e não somente ser autodidata e estudar somente as coisas que o mercado pede?

Nem tudo é trabalho ou dinheiro. Se você tiver condições de se manter na faculdade eu faria e focaria em aprender o máximo possível.

As coisas que o mercado pede sempre vai mudando, você precisa estudar os conceitos que são timeless. Os conceitos não mudam. A base.

Partindo da teoria que a gente aprende muito mais em startups ou empresas, por que não ficar 4 anos em empresas invés ficar 4 anos ou mais em uma graduação?

Ao optar por não cursar uma faculdade, você tem que mostrar para o mundo que você é muito bom. Isso é o caminho mais difícil, mas escala melhor ao longo prazo. É antifragil.

> Você utiliza ainda a parte de exatas da graduação na sua carreira?

Matemática, grafos, algoritmos ainda utilizo diretamente e indiretamente.

Todo conhecimento te ajuda para resolver algum problema novo.

Você tem que focar em coisas que te permitam resolver o maior número de problemas

# Repeat yourself

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/repeat-yourself
Tags: learning, teaching

If you wanna teach someone something you need to repeat yourself

If you wanna something to stick ([Make it stick](./make-it-stick)), this thing should show up more then once.

When doing UX try to show the same action in different places and context, so you can have more chances of the user using it.

When [Learning a new language](./learning-a-new-language), you need to see the same words and structure more than once to remember then. You also need to see them in different context, in a variety ways.

When learning to solve a problem or coding, you need to solve variety of problems with the same concepts to master it

We pass many different training data to machine learning algorithms so they can learn and learn all the variantions. So you can become invariant to changes, much like SIFT algorithm.

SIFT can detect the same image in different orientation, scale,

You want to be `invariant` to be able to transfer the knowledge to other context.

# Resolution

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/resolution
Tags: writing, productivity

We can separate medias in low and high resolution.

Low resolution gives you less detail and you need to fill what is missing with your own context.

High resolution gives you much more detail, so you don't have any misunderstanding

When production content, you can produce using low or high resolution.

I think the first draft of anything should be low resolution

When doing the first version of the code you should not care about all the tiny details, keep the high resolution to the end.

When doing the first design, do the first draft with "low" quality, with less details, maybe even without colors, prefer a wireframe.

When building a house you build first the structure and you finish the house wall paint color in the end

If you try to product both low and high resolution at the same time you going to struggle.

You can think of it as building your content/code/house in layers.

Each layer will have more details, and more resolution than the last one.

# Root Cause Analysis

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/root-cause-analysis
Tags: debugging, typescript

Most developers don't know how to find the root cause of a bug.

The root cause is the "real" cause of a problem.

Let's see any example with typescript, let's see this code:

```ts
const user = await User.findOne();
```

For some reason typescript is inferring user having type any instead of IUser.

If you don't go find the root cause of this, you gonna fix this like this:

```ts
const user: IUser = await User.findOne();
```

now, user has the right type, but if you another developer uses findOne it will be the type any again.

You solved your problem, but you didn't solved the real cause of the problem

The right way to solve this is to ask "why findOne is inferring the wrong type?".

Then you go over mongoose typedefs, and realize that someone made a regression and cause this trouble

So you send a fix to mongoose types, apply a patch-package in your repo, and this is fixed to everybody in your team.

If you don't do this, you gonna propagate the error in the whole codebase

# SaaS

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/saas
Tags: startups, business

#business

SaaS is Software as a Service.

Instead of customer paying an unique time for a software in a box, it pays for a service and the deliver of the software in a daily/monthly basis.

Opposite to [Software House](./software-house) that deliver the software once and that's it.

it is hard to sell a digital good, as the sound industry discovered.

Users will pirate their mp3 to listen to music.

The subscription means that you're going to deliver value over time.

A subscription only makes sense if you keep delivering value over time.

A SaaS uses a subscription as a two way incentive to deliver value over time.

At Entria we started as a [Software House](./software-house) development software for big companies like Natura and Gol.

Then we transitioned to Feedback House, our SaaS product.

SaaS has a Long Term incentive, as we need to keep improving our product to sales to more users and keep current users happy without churning.

- https://divinations.substack.com/p/the-open-podcast-ecosystem-is-dying

# Saving a project on fire

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/saving-a-project-on-fire
Tags: engineering, testing, management

Have you ever been in a project that was on 🔥?

A project is on 🔥when it passed the deadline. When the developer team are put on a "war room" to make sure there is no distractions to finish the project.

The project is on 🔥when there are a lot of basics bugs, like when you click a button it just blow off your application.

The project is on 🔥when new code of a bug fix causes more harm them good, you fix 1 thing to discover you break 2.

It just feel you won't leave this project anymore \\o/.

---

**How to save a project like this?**

To fix a project like this we need 3 things: automation; types and tests;

The first thing to setup is automation: CI/CD.

CI/CD will make sure we always run some tests in an automated way.

it should make sure our dependencies are working well (running yarn install, for instance)

it should make sure our lint is all set.

it should make sure we don't have wrong types.

it should make sure our tests pass.

You also need to setup lint-staged to run pre checks before commiting new code.

Lint-staged will run some checks based on commited files, so you make sure each least these files follow the new code pattern.

Everything should be incremental

You should add more types and tests based on the bugs report.

For each bug you need to improve types and add regression tests to make sure you won't get the same bug again.

To make sure you are moving forward without going backwards.

# Simply

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/simply
Tags: simply

Why most people don't try to come up with the simplest design?

Why most people don't try to use the simplest solution to solve a problem?

Why not use the solution with fewer parameters?

Why not use the smallest code?

Why most people do not try to simplify existing products?

It is easy to sell complexity.
It is easy to sell more features.
It is easy to appear smart to propose a complex solution.
It is easy to write a far-fetched article.

I love mathematics, physics, and science.
They are always trying to explain everything with fewer axioms, with the smallest formulas.
They want to unify many theories into fewer ones.

It is interesting how "simple" things can generate complex systems.
Mandelbrot formula is so simple but generates amazing fractals.
Einstein's Mass-energy Equation is just 3 letters and it is so profound.

When designing something new, always try to come up with the simplest design possible.

When modifying an existing system, try to simplify and reduce entropy before adding new features.

Artificial Inteligence is our best signal-noise filter.
AI will help us simplify everything.
Complexity is entropy and noise.

# Small Batches Sizes

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/small-batches-sizes
Tags: productivity, product-development

Batch is a way to group some actions/things in a group

Prefer to work in small batches.

Prefer to release to production a small batch of issues, and small batch of code to avoid creating a lot of regressions or problems.

Small batch are easier to review.

Prefer work in small batch when writing, write a bit and get early feedback to make sure you are going in the right direction

Machine learning algorithm use a small rate of learning (batch), to make sure it converge to the right solution, if the rate is too big it will go in the wrong direction

Small batches generate a fast [Feedback Loop](./feedback-loop) .

[How to Take Smart Notes](./how-to-take-smart-notes)

WIP Written

[Principles of Product Development Flow](./principles-of-product-development-flow)

---

The benefits of small batch sizes

Reducing your batch size you reduce the cycle time.

Cycle time is the time you take from an issue/task/feature ideation to go to production/live.

The small the batch size the small is your cycle time, and fast you improve your product/service.

The faster you ship new features

The faster you fix bugs.

The faster you add improvement

Reducing your batch size reduces variability of flow.

If one of your sprint has a batch size of 10 issues and the next one has a batch size 60 issues, which one will you deliver faster? If you keep your batch size small you always keep the same flow of delivering.

Reducing batch size accelerates feedbacks

If you have a small batch size you deliver fast and get feedback faster. This will make sure you are building the right thing or find bugs or errors faster. Your errors/failure will also be smaller.

Reducing batch size reduces risk

It is much safe to deliver a few new items/changes then many of them.

Instead of doing one off release of a new feature, try to release it incrementally.

Incrementally you can adjust to changes in requirements, you can adjust to errors during the releases, and you can adjust to feedback.

Reducing batch size reduces overhead

Large batches sizes increases the average number of bugs. If you have 300 open bugs, when you find bug number 301, we need to recheck the other 300 for duplications. For small batch sizes it would have many less number of test to retest if a new bug was found.

Large batches reduces efficiency

You can think of large chunk of work by an individual is more efficiency, but this is only local as reduce the feedback loops and overall efficiency. The individual could put some wrong assumptions and have to redo most of the work done.

Large batches lower motivation and urgency

Large batches dilutes responsibility, as if I'm responsible to deliver 1 modules from 100 modules, I feel much less urgency. It also make more probable of someone delaying one of those modules. It takes to much time to see your work in production and get the feedback from user.

Large batch size increases cost and schedule growth

It is hard to estimate schedule and cost for large batch sizes.

The batch size is limited by its worst element

the batch size will take as long as its worst element, 1 item will delay and make all other cost more.

Good infrastructure enables small batches

If you have CI/CD with tests and deploys all automated, it makes it easier to handle small batches and do many releases on a daily basis

Feature flags can reduce batch size

Feature flags let you deliver new feature faster for a few customer, reducing risks, accelerating feedback loops.

To reduce batch size reduce scope.

Decide to deliver less to deliver faster and in time.

To do wait 100% of the requirement to start designing and coding. these requirement will always change a long the way.

Converging fast to Solutions

Reducing your Batch Sizes

---

# Software House

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/software-house
Tags: startups, business

Software House is a business model where you develop solutions for our companies.

The solutions are tailored per customer needs.

The problem with Software Houses is that you always need to do the same work to earn the same money, there are no compound effects.

It is also a business that does not scale, as you can't sell the same solution to another customer.

One way to reduce the cost of software house is to use Monorepo to try to extract common code in packages and reuse them in new projects, reducing the total cost of the new software.

One good point of Software House is that it generates more money upfront, so it can be good to bootstrap without a VC.

When working in a SH you can starting looking for a good idea to build your SaaS product.

To find good ideas you should read [Where good ideas come from](./where-good-ideas-come-from) .

SH is like a freelance in a group of people.

The incentive of your customer is to reduce the payment for you, and your incentive is to charge more as the project grows.

It usually does not have any tests, as soon as you deliver the project you move to the next one.

There are no long term incentives.

For a better business model check [SaaS](./saas)

---

# Software House and the Prisoner's Dilemma

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/software-house-and-the-prisoner-s-dilemma
Tags: startups, game-theory

Prisoner's dilemma is a classic game theory example where 2 "individuals" might not cooperate.

The 2 "individuals" in the case of this article will be the Software House (SH) and the Customer.

This can also be applied to a freelancer and a customer.

The cooperation action of the SH will be to deliver software with high quality

The betrayal action of the SH will be to deliver software with poor quality

The customer cooperation action will be to keep re-contracting the same SH

The customer betrayal action will be to contract another SH to reduce the service price of another SH.

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner%27s_dilemma
- https://ncase.me/trust/

# Structure

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/structure/structure/structure/structure/structure
Tags: structure

You are probably wondering why the Structure note is inside so many structure.

"The paradox of structure is that, whatever its nature, any structure is both enabling and limiting at the same time"

You need to find the right balance of chaos and structure.

You should add more structure as you grow, as your company grows.

Try to avoid too much structure when it is not needed.

A few examples of too much structure

You decided to use all design patterns that you learned for an application of 1 endpoint.
You created 50 files instead of just 2.

You require 2 approvals for a pull request, even if it is a small change.

---

The more structure you add, the slower you move, more bureaucratic you become.

Do not create a new file if you have too few lines.
Do not create a new folder if you have a few files.
Do not create a complex review process if you have a small team.

Entropy will keep trying to add more and more structure, so you need to fight it.

## References

- [Systems, man, and the paradox of structure](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/1244239)

# Study/Work Backwards

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/study-work-backwards
Tags: learning, product

Steve Jobs said do work backwards

Instead of starting with a technology and see how to sell to customers

Start with customers and see what they need, and what technology fits their needs.

That's way that people struggle with learning by theory.

We can think of theory as the same as technology

We need to work backwards when learning, start with the problem you want to solve.

Them find the right theory that you need to learn to solve the problem.

instead of learning parsers by no reason, wait until the problem shows up for you.

I need to move one package to another, the first thing we need is to understading the imports and exports to make sure we refactor them to the right place.

We need a "parser" to understand raw text.

We also need a subgraph "graph" of dependencies to make sure we move the file and all their dependencies together

# Testing Concept Frontend

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/testing-concept-frontend
Tags: testing, concept, frontend

You first need to undestand the concept of frontend tests.

You should not test the implementation but the behavior

You test like the end user

For instance, imagine a login screen with email and password inputs and a submit button

The test should input the email and the password, then click in the submit button.

You should assert the API was called with the inputted data.

When using testing library you test against DOM

code:

```jsx
const emailInput = getByTestId(emailTestId);
fireEvent.onChange(emailInput, { target: { value: 'email@email.com.br' } });

const passwordInput = getByTestId(passwordTestId);
fireEvent.onChange(passwordInput, { target: { value: 'pwd' } });

const submitButton = getByText('Login').closest('button');
fireEvent.click(submitButton);

// assert api was called properly
```

# Text Formats

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/text-formats
Tags: content, frontend

#content

**Plain Text**

We have a plain text when we don't have any formatting, all text are the same

**Rich Text**

Rich text is when we have formatting for part of the text.

When you enable formatting per part of the text, you need to store text as blocks, and each block has it is own styling.

**Markdown**

Markdown is another text format, with it is own peculiarities.

It has some has predefined "tags" where the user applies format based on text

`## my title` represent a heading 2 text

Markdown is more known by programmers

**How to store rich text data?**

- draft-js uses an json with blocks information
- GraphQL
- Web
- React Native
- Rendered?

**How to present data?**

- You need to process blocks information and output result in html

**Why we need them?**

We need them because users want a rich medium to communicate with other ([Thinking Tools](./thinking-tools) )

It can contains: text, image, video, links, mentions, emojis, gifs and more

# Text vs Video vs Audio

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/text-vs-video-vs-audio
Tags: learning, content

[Information](./information)

Text is low resolution, it let some uncertainty to participants to feel in, it brings more engagement

Audio/Video are more high resolution, it has less uncertainty.

If you are a beginner video/audio is easier to you to follow because they will have more “complete” information.

Text are better to store gists, tl;dr;

It is easier to skim and to compose.

To make read productive you need to be able to control low and high resolution reading, with and without details.

---

What is better to learn?

If you have no knowledge about this subject, try to go for videos/audio first, high resolution to fill most of your basic questions.

Then move to a low res medium to gather more knowledge faster, and fill yourself the uncertainty to [Make it stick](./make-it-stick) better.

[Workshop](./workshop) is a mix of high and low res.

Explanation and introduction to concepts uses high res videos, and exercises are low res to make your mind feel the gaps of [Reality has a lot of details](./reality-has-a-lot-of-details)

# The era of Content Builders

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/the-era-of-content-builders
Tags: content, nocode

#content #builder

## What is Content?

Content is information organized to an audience

## What is a Content Builder?

A content builder is a software that you let organize your content in different ways.

You can present information in different forms, using text with many formatting (bold), using images, using audio (podcasts), using video, using gif, using tables, using text formatting, you can embed content from other websites like twitter, youtube and so on.

Content builder goes from "simple" text editor, to note taking app to mobile site nocode solutions.

## Before content builder?

We have different types of "documents" to present information.

We have Word/Google Docs to present text information.

We have Excel/Google Sheets to present table information

We have Powerpoint/Google Slides to do slides.

What if I want to add some text/paragraph to my sheet?

What if I want to add some slide form to my text document?

## Blocks

We can have basic blocks like simple text and paragraphs

We can have links to other pages, blog posts or people

we can have media (image, embeds, audio, video)

## Working with Blocks

You can copy and paste text, single blocks or multiple blocks

You can reorder blocks, you can edit and duplicate them

You can transform one block into another

## Layouts

Layout are blocks that arrange blocks inside a screen

They are useful when building a website

Most website can be built with predefined layout patterns

## Interactive Blocks

ObservableHQ let you have interactive blocks to document and play with data visualization

You could embed some code playground in your content to make them more interessant

## Examples of Content Builders?

Fluid Framework

Notion

Dropbox Paper

Mdx

Airtable

Observable HQ - https://observablehq.com/

NoCode in general

WebFlow

Canva https://www.canva.com/pt\_br/

Wix

Building Blocks of Content Builder

Similar to building blocks for SaaS (https://sibelius.substack.com/p/where-good-saas-come-from). We can have many building blocks when creating content.

WYSIWYG

what you see is what you get

A [Digital Garden](./digital-garden) is an example of a content builder where you build and modify the blocks.

You decide which blocks to implement based on what your needs. It is the curation of your content and output. If you need to show some code you need a block to handle it properly.

Using the right blocks can make your Writing more interesting to read

This blocks can be thought as tools for thinking

# Time Preference

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/time-preference
Tags: economics, bitcoin

- https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07BPM3GZQ/ref=dp-kindle-redirect?_encoding=UTF8&btkr=1

[Bitcoin](./bitcoin)

Time preference tldr:
If you have 8 hours to catch fishes,
do you use the 8 hours to catch fish or do you use only 6 hours and create a net to catch more fish?
If you do the latter you have a low time preference, it means you value your future more than your present

For developers this would be like, do you use part of your development hours to refactor and improve your code?

If you do freelance you value for the present than the future
If you work in a company/product/SaaS over a long period of time you prefer future over present

A high time preference values present and immediate future

A low time preference values futher future over present

---

**What's your time preference?**

Time preference (long-term orientation) is an economy concept that measure how an individual values the present over future.

A high time preference means that you value more the present then the future.

And a low time preference means that you value more the future over the present.

**A simple example**
If you have 8 hours to catch fishes, do you use the 8 hours to catch fish or do you use only 6 hours and create a net to catch more fish with the rest of 2 hours?
If you do the latter you have a low time preference, it means you value your future more than your present

**Money**

A sound money turns more people to have a low time preference, as the value of the money increases over time, you would prefer to save money instead of spending. Deferred consumptions.

Our current money model based on inflation make people spend more as the money devalues overtime.

**Fitness**

The process to get fit takes a "long" time. You only get fit if your time preference for this is low enough.

You choose to spend your time doing exercises that feel hard to you, but you only get the benefits in the long run.

**Health**

We can apply the same concepts to health, you avoid consuming junk food to have a better life in the future.

**Sofware House vs SaaS**

Software House usually has a high time preference as it prefer to deliver bad/medium quality code to the customer, deliver the product and get a large chunk of money, and move to the next project.

The problem with this model is that SH always need to do the same work to get the same amount of money.

SaaS product charges a much small subscription per customers, but it earns this amount for long periods of time. This also make sure the SaaS company will keep delivering value to current and new customers to keep them paying for the product, the incentives are aligned, it is a win-win relationship.

**Marriage**

Marriage is a long term. If you don't want to spend the rest of your life if the person you are married, you should get a divorce. Marriage gets better in the long run as you get used to each other and trust more each other.

**Habits**

Habits is what you do in a daily basis

atomic habits, exponential, long run, time preference

Notion and Webstorm uses ctrl+\[ and ctrl+\] to be able to go back and forth so you can move around and avoid losing context

Mouse is good, but it is slow as you need to navigate the "whole" screen

the keyboard goes directly to where you wanna go

# Tweet Engagement

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/tweet-engagement
Tags: twitter, audience

[Growth Loops](./growth-loops)

[Standing Ovation](./standing-ovation)

How to make your audience engage?

**Use a question**

When you use a question in your tweet, you are basically asking people (your audience) to answer it

People care about their name, their opinions and everything that they think are their own.

Most people don't start a discussion or tweet because of the [Standing Ovation](./standing-ovation) model, so when tweeting give voice to them to engage and show their opinions.

**Use an image/video/gif or audio**

text is low resolution cold medium ([Hot Cold Media](./hot-cold-media))

sometimes text is not enough to conceive the information because it needs more context to make it sense of it.

**Use buzz word**

buzz word (hashtags) are a great way to find your content

bots can retweet you based on some hashtags

you tweet will show up when people search this hashtag

**Tag some people**

when you tag some people (not in the begin of the tweet - because it will restrict the tweet to only people that follow you and the other people)

your tweet will also reach their audience

Do not tag too many people, and not always the same people, avoid spamming, use with caution.

**External Links**

Make sure external links produces a good social image (og) to improve engagement.

**Share**

Make sure to share your tweet in many places (slack, discord, facebook and other)

Improve your reach

**Relink and Retweet**

When doing a new tweet, try to find related tweets of yours, and relink them in threads

**Threads**

A good thread can improve the value of individual tweets

A group of tweets has more values of all individual tweets

Funny

People like funny things

Meme

Bring image, and gifs to get a hot funny medium

## value over internship

How they make money.

Ask for challenges

Do not limit yourself to your job title, only frontend, only backend.
Learn it all.
Contribute it all.

Bring new ideias with RFC, POCs.

Reduce the work of your Boss

Deliver everything with high quality.

# What should you Build Next?

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/what-should-you-build-next
Tags: product, startups

bug/feature/refactor

A feature is a new capability to the software

You add features when your software can’t handle some users use case

Improvement: improvements are interactions to make an existing feature better. It can make the feature easier to use. It can make the feature faster to use.

Bug: a bug happens when a feature is implemented and not tested properly, or when some edge cases were not considered.

Refactor: it is when we improve the code structure without changing their behavior

---

First principles first

Instead of build a new feature for each user wish, try to understand the core problem they have in their workflows.

Prefer build low level building blocks features that can be reused in many workflows

Try to solve a set of problems instead just one use case.

Prefer a more generic/extensible feature than a much more specific

Do not build for a single user, build for a group of them

---

Basecamp Shape Up

- https://basecamp.com/shapeup

[Principles of Product Development Flow](./principles-of-product-development-flow)

---

You should decide on what to work on based on the cost of delaying it.

How is the cost of delaying fixing this bugs?

How many users are affected by this bug?

Is this bug generating inconsistent data?

Is this bug part of core user workflows?

Can user use the product even with this bug?

How many customer supports ticket will be open because of this bug?

How is the cost of delaying this refactor?

How many more hours developers Will spend before this refactor?

How long will take this refactor?

How this refactor affects the other devs?

What is the risks of this refactor?

Can this refactor be done incrementally?

How is the cost of delaying this improvement?

How many users will perceive this improvement?

How this improvement will affect users?

How many users uses the feature that wil be improved?

How is the cost of delaying this feature?

How many users are waiting this feature?

How this feature helps sales team to sale more?

Is this feature for any user or high usage users?

Will this feature improve usage and engagement?

[The Nonesuch Beast](./the-nonesuch-beast)

For Uber work well, we need a good mobile phone hardware with GPS, we also need a good broad brand connection.

# work study life balance

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/work-study-life-balance
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## work study life balance

"What strategies do you suggest for balancing ongoing technology learning with the demands of work and personal life?"

The best way is to align your work with what you want to learn.

For instance, if you want to study more React, the best way is to get a job that uses React every day.

You will get paid to study and learn what you are looking for.

If you can't do that in your current job, you have some options.

You can introduce this new technology in your work if this makes sense.
Write an RFC (Request For Comments) showing all the benefits of this new technology for the company current tech stack.
Do a simple POC (Proof of Concept).

You can get another job that uses this new tech.

You can get a freelancer to learn more this new tech.

You just need to be able to learn fast until they figure it out that you don't have everything figure it out.

To balance your work with your life, you need to work in something that you believe.
You need to optimize and automate the work, so you can be able to be very productive and work for 6/8 hours.
Working extra time can be useful in the beginning of the carrer so you can grow faster.
Always work hard for yourself.
Every time you are working on something more hours, and you are learning a lot, it is good for your carrer and for your company.

## References

- [Scaling Engineering Teams via RFCs: Writing Things Down](https://blog.pragmaticengineer.com/scaling-engineering-teams-via-writing-things-down-rfcs/)

---

# work visibility

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/mentorship/work-visibility
Tags: advice, mentorship, questions, async

## work visibility

"Are there specific strategies to increase the visibility and recognition of my work within the company where I will be interning?"

It is the same way that you get your work visible outside your company.
You use Learn in public.
You share all the work you are doing in public, in public channels, in articles, at open source.

You write down everything you are contributing to the company, brag document.
Your manage can forget what you did, but you should not. You should let know how you are contributing to the company.

You need to prove that your work contributions are moving the metrics that matters.
Does your work reduces costs? increase revenue? simplify onboarding? reduces CACs ? make team ship faster?

"It's better to appear honest than to be honest"

You need to market your work. Only work or coding is not enough, you need to demo, present to other areas.

## References

- [Learn in Public](https://www.swyx.io/learn-in-public)
- [Brag Documents](https://jvns.ca/blog/brag-documents/)
- [Becoming a Go To person gets you](https://careercutler.substack.com/p/becoming-a-go-to-person-gets-you)

# Workshop

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/workshop
Tags: learning, teaching

- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4RjXHY3w0Jg&feature=emb_title
- https://egghead.io/lessons/egghead-use-zoom-for-kcd-workshops
- https://github.com/kentcdodds/react-fundamentals

Workshop is a set of practical exercises so users really "taste" how to solve something

They need to struggle to solve at first to improve learning retaintion

Zoom has a breakout room divides the people of a workshop in many rooms so they can discuss in smaller groups while solving exercises

Kent has 3 types of workshops

- set of exercises
- fill parts of a complete app
- build an app incrementally

Each exercise can have an extra credit for advanced students

You need to cap to 30/40 people per workshop so you can have time to help all students, more active learning instead of passing learning of a webinar

# you can do anything, but you can't do everything

ou reduce the scope, of what are you working on, -> You reduce the scope of what are you working on,

- https://medium.com/astella-investimentos/di%C3%A1rio-de-um-vc-rumo-%C3%A0-conquista-do-universo-68aabe360c90

Esse texto fala sobre a importância do foco tb

A verdade é que focar não é algo fácil de se fazer. Primeiro porque cognitivamente somos feitos para _hedgear_ nossas apostas e assim aumentar nossas chances de sobrevivência. Segundo porque muitos desconhecem a história das empresas que realmente escalam. Terceiro porque tendemos a temer os competidores e achar que é melhor conquistar tudo de uma vez. Quarto, porque mesmo que eu acredite no foco, eu preciso convencer todo o meu time e as vezes investidores também. E por fim, muitas vezes não temos tempo nem dinheiro suficiente para sobreviver, e aí a única saída é vender para qualquer um que aparecer.

---

May talk about Planning and goals, I understand the example and context, but the focus needs to be aggregated to some other things. If you are focused in wrong things you don´t get much success. Maybe mentoring be interesting at this point.

Think about the utility and needs – Prospect theory and expected utility hypothesis
The expected utility hypothesis serves as a reference guide for decisions when the return is uncertain. The theory recommends which option rational individuals should choose in a complex situation, based on their risk appetite and preferences.
So, you got some risk e take some decision with some racional thinking. In another way, general people have the decision affected by the perspective, for example:

Prospect theory suggests that; When faced with a risky choice leading to gains agents are risk averse, preferring the certain outcome with a lower expected utility.

People are loss averse and prefer to remain in an inert state, this works as an internal risk policy and a reactive mental defense state. Changing mental focus requires rational, deliberative, and logical decision making. With human evolution, our body was shaped to pulp energy. Although often a person is guided with advice or suggestion about their activities and focus, change needs a prior non-intuitive rational deliberation that requires discipline, flexibility and willingness to change. Every change has a risk

Risk diversification and regression toward the mean

Defining strategy and efficient thinking, only diversifying the approaches will make you similar to the others in the market. It is important to diversify while maintaining a balance between efficiency and scale. Although it is necessary to make a quick mistake to understand the market and customers, it takes agility, knowledge, focus and competence to equate the company's progress and flow in the opportunities generated with scale.

It should have a dynamic pricing model, where the salesforce man is part of the business strategy from the beginning. As it is a disruption of the sales model, the professional's work model must be differentiated.

# You may not need to buy this course?

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/you-may-not-need-to-buy-this-course
Tags: learning

Buying a course make your feel that you made a real commitment to learn something.

Watching the videos also make you feel you are making progress.

The problem start happening when you try to apply everything that you "learned" in a side project, or real life.

Usually what happens is that things are not so easy as it sounds in a video lesson, you try to setup Webpack and get weird error that didn't show in the video.

Reality has many more details that you can see in video.

All courses are about happy case. The happy case is when everything goes well.

The problem is that not everything goes well at first in real life. As your computer could be a bit difference. The version of the package you are working on is different.

So if courses are not the best way to learn something, what is the best one?

**Better ways to learn something**

Learning and cognitive process has being studied many and many years, and we still do not an answer of how we learn.

One book that has many insights about it is Make it Stick.

- https://www.amazon.com.br/Make-Stick-Science-Successful-Learning/dp/0674729013

You learn better if you connect new concepts to old ones that you know already.

You learn more practicing

[Make it stick](./make-it-stick)

---

# Zettelkasten for Design

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/zettelkasten-for-design
Tags: zettelkasten, design

#organization #design

Zettelkasten is a way to organize ideas in atoms that can be joined and combined.

What would be like a zettelkasten for design?

We should be able to link one design to another

We should be able to compose designs using other design atoms.

# Zettelkasten Notion

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/zettelkasten-notion
Tags: zettelkasten, notion

#zettelkasten #notion #implementation

How to implement zettelkasten process in notion?

- use a database
- use a template for a new zettle
- add backlinks

Zettelkasten in notion: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2tttUPGlB8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2tttUPGlB8)

My Zettelkasten in Notion

I have a list of notes inside a knowledge base note

All notes are flat, I keep external links and links to other notes inside each note

I create a note with some concepts and then one note per concept

For instance, reading a blog/book I create a note for the book and N notes per each concept

I also have notes about practice.

Practice is the only way to learn about the details of reality [Reality has a lot of details](./reality-has-a-lot-of-details) .

# Zine

URL: https://sibelius.github.io/zettelkasten/notes/zine
Tags: content

#content #image #text

Zine is a type of content used a lot by Julia Evans where she puts some tips and content in a single image with text.

It is a tl;dr; based on image + text, a cartoon based approach to convey information.
